en.editorNote: For the friend forever chasing a 'better self' who still never feels like enough. Also good right after you've set a pile of new goals and started resenting your current self — take a breath first.
variations: Without self-acceptance, even getting better still feels like something's missing.
Growth is meant to be kind to you, not a punishment for who you are now.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'your value is inherent, not earned by productivity' self-worth theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
休息不用先賺到。
你不是機器，沒有「產能」達標才准喘氣這回事。
累了就停，這件事本身就夠正當了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一放假就有罪惡感、非得做點什麼才安心的朋友。也適合你躺著滑手機、卻一直被「該起來做正事」念頭追著跑的時候。
variations: 你不是靠有沒有用來決定值不值得休息的。
允許自己什麼都不做，也是一種對自己好。

en.content:
You don't have to earn rest.
You're not a machine that only gets to breathe once it hits a quota.
Being tired is reason enough to stop.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels guilty the moment they take a day off and has to be doing something to feel okay. Also good when you're lying down scrolling but keep getting chased by the 'get up and be productive' voice.
variations: Your worth isn't measured by how useful you were today.
Letting yourself do nothing is a way of being kind to yourself too.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'stop comparing, run your own race' self-love theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
別人開得快，不代表你走錯路。
每個人的時區本來就不一樣，
你按自己的步調前進，也算數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一打開 IG 看到同齡人又升遷又結婚，就開始否定自己的朋友。也適合你覺得「大家都超前、只有我卡住」的深夜。
variations: 你不是慢，你只是走在自己的時間裡。
花有花的花期，你急著開，反而開不好。

en.content:
Someone moving faster doesn't mean you took a wrong turn.
Everyone runs on a different clock —
moving at your own pace still counts.
en.editorNote: For the friend who opens Instagram, sees peers getting promoted and married, and instantly starts doubting themselves. Also good for those late nights when it feels like everyone's ahead and you're the only one stuck.
variations: You're not behind. You're just on your own timeline.
Every flower has its season. Rush the bloom and it won't come out right.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'love yourself enough to set boundaries' theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
會讓你有罪惡感的界線，通常正是你最需要的那一條。
拒絕別人不代表你壞，
只代表你終於把自己也算進去了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種永遠不敢說「不」、怕拒絕別人就會被討厭的朋友。也適合你剛拒絕完一個過分的請求、正在心虛的那五分鐘。
variations: 你不是變冷漠了，你只是不再免費消耗自己。
設界線會不舒服，是因為你以前太習慣委屈。

en.content:
The boundary that makes you feel guilty is usually the one you needed most.
Saying no doesn't make you a bad person —
it just means you finally counted yourself in too.
en.editorNote: For the friend who can never say no and is scared that turning someone down means being disliked. Also good for the guilty five minutes right after you've declined an unreasonable request.
variations: You didn't get colder. You just stopped running on empty for free.
Boundaries feel uncomfortable because you were too used to shrinking.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you don't have to earn rest' / 'worth not tied to productivity' affirmations; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
休息不用先賺來。
你不是機器，累了就停，
不是因為做完了什麼，只是因為你是人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一放假就焦慮、覺得沒生產力就沒價值的工作狂朋友。也適合你躺在沙發上卻一直想著「我是不是該做點正事」的週末午後。
variations: 你的價值不是用產出來計算的。
先休息，罪惡感等一下再說。

en.content:
You don't have to earn rest.
You're not a machine — you stop because you're tired,
not because you finished something, just because you're human.
en.editorNote: For the workaholic friend who gets anxious the moment they have a day off and feels worthless without being productive. Also for the weekend afternoon when you're lying on the couch but can't stop thinking you should be doing something 'real'.
variations: Your worth isn't measured in output.
Rest first. The guilt can wait.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'give yourself the compassion you give others' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你把最溫柔的話都留給別人，
卻用最狠的話對自己。
今天開始，也分一點溫柔給自己吧。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種對朋友超好、對自己超嚴格的人。也適合你又在半夜檢討自己、把一整天的小失誤放大成人格缺陷的時候。
variations: 你對別人那麼寬容，也值得對自己寬容一次。
如果朋友犯這個錯，你會這樣罵他嗎？不會，那就別罵自己。

en.content:
You save your gentlest words for everyone else,
then use the cruelest ones on yourself.
Starting today, spare a little of that kindness for you too.
en.editorNote: For the person who's endlessly kind to friends but brutally hard on themselves. Also for those nights when you replay every small slip-up and blow it up into a character flaw.
variations: You're so forgiving with others. You deserve to be forgiven once too.
If a friend made this mistake, would you talk to them like that? No — so don't talk to yourself like that.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'protecting my peace' self-love theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
保護自己的平靜，不需要跟任何人解釋。
有些人你不用討厭，
只是不用再讓他們住進你腦子裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種被某段關係反覆消耗、卻還在自責「是不是我太小題大作」的朋友。也適合你決定不再回某個訊息、想斷開某段內耗的那一刻。
variations: 你可以祝他好，然後轉身走遠。
把腦子的房間空出來，只留給讓你安心的人。

en.content:
Protecting your peace doesn't require anyone's explanation.
Some people you don't have to hate —
you just stop letting them live rent-free in your head.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps getting drained by one relationship yet still blames themselves for 'overreacting'. Also for the moment you decide not to reply to a certain text and cut loose from something that's been eating at you.
variations: You can wish them well and still walk away.
Clear out the rooms in your head. Keep them for the people who make you feel safe.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'rest without guilt' self-love theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
休息不用先把事情做完才配得到。
累了就先躺平，
世界不會因為你停下來就崩塌。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一放假就有罪惡感、覺得「沒生產力就是在浪費生命」的朋友。也適合你明明累爆了，卻還在硬撐、逼自己再多做一點的那個下午。
variations: 你不是機器，不用 24 小時都在運轉。
先照顧好自己，待辦清單明天還會在那裡等你。

en.content:
You don't have to finish everything before you're allowed to rest.
Tired? Lie down first.
The world won't fall apart just because you paused.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels guilty the moment they take a day off, like being unproductive is wasting their life. Also for the afternoon when you're completely wiped but keep pushing yourself to do just a little more.
variations: You're not a machine. You don't have to run 24/7.
Take care of yourself first — the to-do list will still be there tomorrow.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'worthiness isn't earned' self-love theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
別再等自己「夠好」才願意愛自己。
你的價值不是靠成績、身材或成就換來的，
它從你出生那天就在了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種老是覺得「等我瘦下來、等我升職、等我變厲害再說」的朋友。也適合你又在拿自己跟別人比、覺得現在的自己不值得被善待的時候。
variations: 你不用先變厲害，才有資格喜歡自己。
價值不是考出來的，是你本來就有的。

en.content:
Stop waiting until you're 'good enough' to love yourself.
Your worth isn't traded for grades, a body, or achievements —
it's been there since the day you were born.
en.editorNote: For the friend stuck in 'once I lose the weight, once I get promoted, once I'm better' mode. Also for when you're comparing yourself to others and feel like the current you doesn't deserve any kindness.
variations: You don't have to become impressive first to be allowed to like yourself.
Worth isn't something you test into. You already have it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion affirmations for hard days; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
日子很難的時候，對自己溫柔一點。
你不用假裝沒事，
光是撐到現在，就已經很努力了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給正在低潮、什麼都提不起勁的朋友。也適合你今天只是「活著」就用盡全力、卻還在怪自己不夠積極的那種日子。
variations: 撐到今天的你，已經很勇敢了。
不用馬上好起來，慢慢來也可以。

en.content:
On the hard days, be gentle with yourself.
You don't have to pretend you're fine —
just making it this far already took a lot.
en.editorNote: For a friend in a low patch who can't muster energy for anything. Also for the kind of day when simply staying alive drained everything you had, yet you're still scolding yourself for not doing more.
variations: Making it to today already makes you brave.
You don't have to feel better right away. Slow is okay too.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by inner-critic self-judgment self-love theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
你腦子裡那個一直罵你的聲音，
不是事實，只是習慣。
你可以練習，把它換成一句「沒關係，我在」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種老是自我攻擊、一犯錯就把自己貶到底的朋友。也適合你半夜又被腦內小劇場疲勞轟炸、需要有人幫你按暫停的時候。
variations: 自我檢討不等於自我懲罰。
那個聲音不是你，你可以選擇不聽它的。

en.content:
That voice in your head that keeps tearing you down
isn't the truth — it's just a habit.
You can practice swapping it for one line: 'It's okay, I've got you.'
en.editorNote: For the friend who constantly attacks themselves and spirals into self-loathing over one mistake. Also for those late nights when the mental replay won't stop and you need someone to hit pause for you.
variations: Self-reflection isn't the same as self-punishment.
That voice isn't you. You get to choose not to listen to it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Paulo Coelho 'saying yes to others while saying no to yourself' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
每一次對別人說「好」，
記得看一眼，你是不是同時對自己說了「不」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種永遠把別人的需求排在前面、忘記問自己想不想的人。貼在待辦清單旁邊，答應事情前先看一眼剛剛好。
variations: 把自己排第一，不是自私，是你也是一個人。
你不是無限量供應的，該省著點給。

en.content:
Every time you say 'yes' to someone else,
take a look — are you quietly saying 'no' to yourself?
en.editorNote: For the person who always puts everyone else's needs first and forgets to ask what they actually want. Stick it next to your to-do list — a good glance before you agree to one more thing.
variations: Putting yourself first isn't selfish. You're a person too.
You're not an unlimited supply. Spend yourself a little more carefully.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Max Lucado 'you are valuable simply because you exist' theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
你的價值不用靠做了什麼來證明。
光是你這個人存在，就已經算數了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一沒生產力就覺得自己沒用的朋友。也適合你躺平耍廢一整天、又開始有罪惡感的時候，提醒你休息不用先賺來。
variations: 你不是一台機器，不用靠產出來換取被愛。
什麼都沒做的你，一樣值得。

en.content:
Your worth doesn't need proving by what you get done.
You existing at all — that already counts.
en.editorNote: For the friend who feels useless the moment they stop being productive. Also for the day you did nothing but lie around and the guilt starts creeping in — rest isn't something you have to earn first.
variations: You're not a machine. You don't have to earn love with output.
The you who did nothing today is worth just as much.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Sharon Salzberg 'you deserve your own love and affection' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你花了那麼多力氣去愛別人、擔心別人，
偶爾也把那份溫柔，留一點給自己吧。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合送給那種對誰都很好、就是對自己很兇的朋友。也適合你照顧完全世界、回到家發現自己空空的那個夜晚。
variations: 你也在你要照顧的名單上，別老是把自己漏掉。
對自己好一點，這件事你也有資格。

en.content:
You spend so much energy loving and worrying about everyone else —
now and then, save a little of that tenderness for yourself.
en.editorNote: For the friend who's gentle with everyone but brutal to themselves. Also for the night you've taken care of the whole world and come home to find yourself running on empty.
variations: You're on the list of people you're supposed to take care of too. Stop leaving yourself off it.
Being kind to yourself — you're allowed that one too.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Brené Brown boundaries-as-self-love theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
設界線不是把人推開，
是替自己留一個能好好呼吸的位置。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一被拜託就不敢說不的朋友。也適合你答應完又後悔、覺得自己被榨乾的那個當下，提醒你拒絕別人不等於壞人。
variations: 會讓你委屈到喘不過氣的關係，說不也沒關係。
你有權利守住那條線，就算對方不開心。

en.content:
Setting a boundary isn't pushing people away —
it's keeping a spot where you can actually breathe.
en.editorNote: For the friend who can never say no once they're asked. Also for the moment right after you agreed to something and instantly regretted it — turning someone down doesn't make you the bad guy.
variations: If a relationship leaves you gasping, saying no is allowed.
You're allowed to hold that line, even if they don't like it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you are just as worthy as anyone else' worthiness affirmation; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你跟任何人一樣值得被愛，
這件事不用排隊，也不用比賽。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一滑手機就開始覺得自己不如別人的朋友。也適合你又在跟同學、同事偷偷比較的夜晚，提醒你價值不是拿來排名的。
variations: 別人過得好，不代表你就少了一塊。
你的份，本來就有你的名字，不用搶。

en.content:
You're every bit as worthy of love as anyone else —
no queue to wait in, no contest to win.
en.editorNote: For the friend who starts feeling less-than the second they open their phone. Also for the night you catch yourself quietly measuring up against a classmate or coworker — worth was never a leaderboard.
variations: Someone else doing well doesn't mean there's less of you.
Your share already has your name on it. No need to fight for it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Oscar Wilde 'loving yourself is the beginning of a lifelong romance'; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
跟自己好好相處，
是一場可以談一輩子的戀愛。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一單身就慌、一個人就覺得空的朋友。也適合你剛結束一段關係、重新學著自己過日子的時候，提醒你最長情的對象其實是自己。
variations: 會陪你到最後的那個人，一直都在鏡子裡。
先學會跟自己約會，再談別的也不遲。

en.content:
Getting along with yourself
is one romance that can last your whole life.
en.editorNote: For the friend who panics the moment they're single and feels hollow when they're alone. Also for the season right after a breakup, when you're relearning how to live on your own — the longest relationship you'll ever have is with you.
variations: The person who stays till the very end has always been in the mirror.
Learn to take yourself on a date first. The rest can wait.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'gentleness isn't weakness, it's treating yourself well' healing theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
對自己溫柔不是變軟弱，
是你終於肯停止對自己動手。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種對誰都很有耐心、就是最兇自己的朋友。也適合你又在心裡罵自己「怎麼這麼廢」的時候，提醒你那把最利的刀一直握在自己手上。
variations: 你可以放下那把一直指著自己的刀了。
溫柔對待自己，是需要練習的勇敢。

en.content:
Being gentle with yourself isn't going soft —
it's finally putting down the fists you keep aiming inward.
en.editorNote: For the friend who's endlessly patient with everyone but themselves. Also for the moment you catch yourself thinking 'why am I so useless' — the sharpest blade in the room has been in your own hand the whole time.
variations: You're allowed to lower the knife you keep pointing at yourself.
Being kind to yourself is a kind of brave that takes practice.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'the more you love yourself, the less you need to rely on others'; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你越懂得疼自己，
就越不會把整顆心押在別人身上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一沒人回訊息就開始不安的朋友。也適合你發現自己太在意某個人、快把自己弄丟的時候，提醒你先把自己接住，別人才是加分。
variations: 把自己填滿了，別人的忽冷忽熱就傷不到你。
你不是缺一個人，你是缺一點對自己的溫柔。

en.content:
The more you learn to look after yourself,
the less you bet your whole heart on someone else.
en.editorNote: For the friend who spirals the second a text goes unanswered. Also for the moment you realize you're so wrapped up in someone you're losing yourself — catch yourself first, and everyone else becomes a bonus.
variations: Fill your own cup and their hot-and-cold stops being able to hurt you.
You're not missing a person. You're missing a little tenderness toward yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'boundaries are not selfish, they are self-love' theme; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
說一次「不」，
是給自己留了一整個「好」的空間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種不好意思拒絕別人、最後把自己累垮的朋友。也適合你又要硬著頭皮答應不想做的事之前，提醒你拒絕別人不是壞，是先照顧自己。
variations: 你不欠任何人一個「勉強的答應」。
劃下界線不是把人推開，是把自己留下。

en.content:
Every 'no' you say
clears a whole room for the 'yes' that's actually yours.
en.editorNote: For the friend who can't bear to turn anyone down and ends up running on empty. Also for the moment you're about to grit your teeth and agree to something you dread — saying no isn't unkind, it's putting yourself first.
variations: You don't owe anyone a reluctant yes.
Drawing a line isn't pushing people away — it's keeping yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'your worth doesn't grow with what you acquire' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你的價值不會因為多做了什麼而變高，
它從你出生那天就已經滿分了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一直逼自己更好、卻永遠覺得不夠的朋友。也適合你又在用成就換自我肯定的時候，提醒你不用考到滿分才配被自己愛。
variations: 你不是達標才有價值，你本來就是。
別再拿履歷證明你值得活得好。

en.content:
Your worth doesn't climb with everything you achieve —
it's been full marks since the day you were born.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps pushing to be better and still never feels like enough. Also for the moment you're trading accomplishments for self-approval — you don't need a perfect score to deserve your own love.
variations: You're not worth something once you hit the target. You always were.
Stop using your résumé to prove you deserve a good life.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'this chapter is called protecting my peace' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
從今天起，
你的平靜不再開放給誰隨便打擾。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種常被別人情緒勒索、心情跟著別人起伏的朋友。也適合你決定不再回應那些消耗你的訊息時，給自己一個關門的勇氣。
variations: 保護好自己的心情，也是一種正經事。
不是每個敲門的人，都值得你開門。

en.content:
Starting today,
your peace is no longer open for anyone to walk into.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose mood rides the waves of everyone else's drama. Also for the moment you decide to stop answering the messages that drain you — give yourself permission to close the door.
variations: Protecting your own calm counts as important business.
Not everyone who knocks has earned the right to come in.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'self-love is action, not a feeling' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
愛自己不是一種心情，
是你今天願不願意早點睡、好好吃飯的那些小決定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種嘴上說要愛自己、卻熬夜又亂吃的朋友。也適合你發現自己又在虐待身體的時候，提醒你愛自己是動詞，要一天一天做出來。
variations: 愛自己不是喊口號，是把水喝完、把燈關掉。
你怎麼對待自己的身體，就是你多愛自己的答案。

en.content:
Loving yourself isn't a mood —
it's the small calls you make today: sleep earlier, eat a real meal.
en.editorNote: For the friend who preaches self-care but stays up late and skips meals. Also for the moment you catch yourself running your body into the ground — self-love is a verb, built one day at a time.
variations: Self-love isn't a slogan. It's finishing the water and turning off the light.
How you treat your body is the honest answer to how much you love yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you don't have to sacrifice yourself or stop your steps for anyone' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你不必為了誰，
把自己活得越來越小。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種在感情或關係裡一直退讓、快把自己弄不見的朋友。也適合你又在為了配合別人而收起夢想的時候，提醒你縮小自己換來的和平，撐不了多久。
variations: 別為了留住一個人，把自己折成他喜歡的形狀。
你可以愛人，但不用因此消失。

en.content:
You don't have to shrink yourself
smaller and smaller just to fit beside someone.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps giving ground in a relationship until they nearly disappear. Also for the moment you're folding away your own dreams to accommodate someone — peace bought by making yourself small never lasts.
variations: Don't fold yourself into the shape someone likes just to keep them.
You can love someone without vanishing to do it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'stop apologizing for existing / you deserve to take up space' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你不用為了自己的存在道歉。
這個世界，本來就有你的位置。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種講話前先說「不好意思」、連坐下都要縮著身體的朋友。也適合你又在為了「會不會太麻煩別人」而把自己藏起來的時候，提醒你：佔一點空間，不是罪。
variations: 別再把「不好意思」掛嘴邊，你又沒做錯什麼。
你不是來借住這個世界的，你本來就屬於這裡。

en.content:
You don't owe anyone an apology for existing.
This world has a place for you — it always did.
en.editorNote: For the friend who says 'sorry' before every sentence and shrinks even while sitting down. Also for the moment you're hiding yourself so you won't 'be a bother' — taking up space isn't a crime.
variations: Stop leading with 'sorry.' You didn't do anything wrong.
You're not a guest here. You belong.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Brianna Wiest 'love yourself enough to set boundaries' theme; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
夠愛自己的人，才畫得出界線。
你的時間和力氣很珍貴，該由你決定要給誰。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種不敢拒絕別人、把行事曆塞滿別人的事的朋友。也適合你又想勉強答應某個聚會之前，先問自己：這是我想去的，還是我怕拒絕？畫界線不是冷漠，是把自己算進去。
variations: 拒絕別人不會讓你變壞人，只會讓你剩下力氣愛自己。
你的「不要」，也是一種對自己的溫柔。

en.content:
Loving yourself is what lets you draw the line.
Your time and energy are precious — you get to choose who gets them.
en.editorNote: For the friend who can't say no and fills their calendar with everyone else's plans. Also for the moment before you force a yes to some gathering — ask whether you actually want to go, or you're just scared to decline. A boundary isn't coldness; it's counting yourself in.
variations: Saying no doesn't make you the bad guy. It just leaves you enough to love yourself.
Your 'no' is a kindness too — to you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I am enough and I don't need to change' affirmation; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你已經夠好了，
不是「等你變成別人以後」才夠好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一直覺得「再瘦五公斤、再賺多一點才配快樂」的朋友。也適合你又在拿自己跟別人比較的深夜，提醒你：你要的不是變成另一個人，是好好認識現在這個你。
variations: 你不是半成品，不用等修好才值得被愛。
夠好，是現在式，不是等你達標的未來式。

en.content:
You're already enough —
not 'enough once you turn into someone else.'
en.editorNote: For the friend who thinks they'll only deserve happiness after losing five kilos or earning a bit more. Also for the late night when you're comparing yourself to everyone — you don't need to become another person, just to actually meet the one you are now.
variations: You're not a half-finished draft. You don't have to be fixed to be loved.
'Enough' is present tense, not a future you have to earn.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I don't need to explain every decision or accept every invitation to an argument; keep your light' affirmation; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你不必解釋每個決定，
也不用接下每一場想吵架的邀約。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種被酸一句就急著辯解、被激一下就跳進去吵的朋友。也適合你又想在留言區回那個不懷好意的人之前，先深呼吸——不是每個問題都需要你回答，護住自己的光，比贏一場架重要。
variations: 別人遞來的每一根引線，你都有權不接。
沉默有時候不是輸，是你決定把力氣留給自己。

en.content:
You don't have to explain every decision,
or accept every invitation to a fight.
en.editorNote: For the friend who scrambles to justify themselves at one jab and dives into every argument they're baited into. Also for the moment before you reply to that bad-faith commenter — breathe first. Not every question is yours to answer; guarding your light beats winning the fight.
variations: Every fuse someone hands you, you're allowed to not light.
Silence isn't always losing. Sometimes it's you keeping your energy for yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Yung Pueblo 'you were born enough, you do not need to become enough'; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你出生的時候就已經夠了，
不需要「變成什麼」以後才算數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一直覺得要先達成某個目標、才配得上快樂的朋友。也適合你又開始追一個永遠拉遠的標準時，停下來想想：你不是在等及格，你本來就在名單上。
variations: 你不是要證明給誰看，你本來就已經算數了。
「夠好」不是終點線，是你出發前就帶著的。

en.content:
You were already enough the day you were born —
you don't have to 'become' something to count.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps thinking they'll only deserve happiness after hitting some goal. Also for when you're chasing a bar that keeps moving away — you're not waiting to pass. You were on the list all along.
variations: You don't have anything to prove. You already count.
'Enough' isn't a finish line — it's what you brought with you from the start.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Robert Holden 'no amount of self-improvement can make up for a lack of self-acceptance'; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
再多的自我改進，
也補不上一句「我接受現在的自己」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一直買課、一直立目標、想把自己「修好」的朋友。也適合你又覺得「等我變更好就會喜歡自己」的時候——先接受，再改變，順序反了會一直很累。
variations: 你可以想變更好，同時也喜歡現在的自己，這兩件事不衝突。
改進是加分題，接受自己才是那張及格的底。

en.content:
No amount of self-improvement
can fill the gap left by never accepting yourself.
en.editorNote: For the friend who keeps buying courses and setting goals to 'fix' themselves. Also for when you catch yourself thinking 'I'll like myself once I'm better' — acceptance comes first, then change. Reverse the order and you'll stay exhausted.
variations: You can want to grow and like who you are right now. Those two don't cancel out.
Improvement is the bonus round. Accepting yourself is the passing grade underneath it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'sometimes self-love is choosing to rest without guilt' affirmation; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
有時候最愛自己的方式，
就是允許自己休息，而且不覺得抱歉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種累到不行還硬撐、覺得停下來就是偷懶的朋友。也適合你又想撐過一個不該撐的夜晚時——休息不是欠誰的，你不用為了喘口氣道歉。
variations: 累了就停，這不是放棄，是保養。
休息不用等你「值得」，你需要的時候就可以。

en.content:
Sometimes the most loving thing you can do for yourself
is to rest — and not feel sorry about it.
en.editorNote: For the friend who pushes through total exhaustion because stopping feels like slacking. Also for the night you're about to power through one you shouldn't — rest isn't a debt you owe anyone. You don't have to apologize for catching your breath.
variations: Stop when you're tired. That's not quitting, it's maintenance.
You don't have to 'earn' rest. You're allowed to take it the moment you need it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'gratitude for function — what does my body let me do today' body-image practice; fully rewritten

zh-tw.content:
你的身體不是拿來被看的，
是拿來陪你走完這一天的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在試衣間照鏡子照到心情變差的時候看一眼。也適合傳給那個老是在批評自己身材的朋友——把問題從「它好不好看」換成「它今天陪我做了什麼」，感覺會差很多。
variations: 先謝謝它今天帶你去了哪裡，再來討論它好不好看。
它扛著你過了這麼多年，你至少可以不要再罵它。

en.content:
Your body isn't here to be looked at.
It's here to carry you through the day.
en.editorNote: For the fitting-room moment when the mirror ruins your mood. Also for the friend who never stops criticizing her own shape — swapping 'how does it look' for 'what did it do for me today' changes more than you'd think.
variations: Thank it for where it took you today before you rate how it looks.
It's carried you this far. The least you can do is stop insulting it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the comparison-interrupt reframe ('she looks great, and so do I in my own way'); rewritten as a two-truths line

zh-tw.content:
她很好，這是真的。
你也很好，這也是真的。
這兩件事從來就不用互相扣分。
zh-tw.editorNote: 滑限動滑到心裡發酸的時候可以拿出來讀。重點不是叫你別羨慕別人，是提醒你：別人得幾分，跟你得幾分，根本不是同一張考卷。
variations: 羨慕別人可以，但不用順便扣自己的分。
別人發光，不會讓你變暗，你們又不是同一顆燈泡。

en.content:
She's great. That's true.
You're great too. Also true.
Those two facts have never had to cancel each other out.
en.editorNote: Read this the next time a scroll through Instagram leaves a sour taste. The point isn't to stop admiring people — it's to notice that their score and your score were never on the same test.
variations: You can admire someone without docking points from yourself.
Someone else shining doesn't dim you. You're not wired to the same switch.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'self-compassion pause' practice (hand on heart, one breath, one kind sentence); rewritten as a quote

zh-tw.content:
下次又開始鑽牛角尖的時候，
把手放在胸口，深吸一口氣，
然後對自己說一句你會對朋友說的話。
zh-tw.editorNote: 很土，但真的有用。焦慮上來的時候腦袋是講不贏自己的，先讓身體慢下來，話才聽得進去。適合存起來，在半夜睡不著、腦內小劇場開演的時候用。
variations: 手放在心口，先呼吸，再想事情。
當你開始對自己說重話，先停三秒，換成你會對朋友說的那句。

en.content:
Next time the spiral starts,
put a hand on your chest, take one slow breath,
and say to yourself what you'd say to a friend.
en.editorNote: Corny, but it works. You can't out-argue your own anxiety — you slow the body down first, and then the words land. Worth saving for 2 a.m. when your brain starts screening its greatest hits.
variations: Hand on your heart. Breathe first, think second.
The moment you start talking down to yourself, pause three seconds and swap in what you'd tell a friend.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'you hold yourself to a standard you'd never hold anyone else to' theme; rewritten

zh-tw.content:
如果你用對自己的那套標準去要求別人，
你大概早就沒有朋友了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種對全世界都很寬容、只對自己特別狠的人。不是要你降低標準，是提醒你：你為自己訂的規則，如果拿去套在別人身上你自己都會覺得太過分，那它本來就不合理。
variations: 你對自己講的話，如果對朋友講，人家會封鎖你。
同一件事，你原諒了所有人，就是不肯放過自己。

en.content:
If you held other people to the standard you hold yourself to,
you'd have run out of friends years ago.
en.editorNote: For the person who extends endless grace to everyone but themselves. It's not about lowering the bar — it's about noticing that a rule you'd consider cruel applied to anyone else was never a fair rule to begin with.
variations: If you said to a friend what you say to yourself, they'd block you.
Same mistake, and you've forgiven everyone involved except you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'common humanity' component of self-compassion (everyone struggles, you're not uniquely broken); rewritten

zh-tw.content:
你以為只有你活得一團亂，
其實你羨慕的那些人，
只是沒有把重來的那幾次貼出來而已。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合覺得「大家都上軌道了只有我還在原地」的那種夜晚。你看到的是別人的成果頁，不是他的草稿。搞砸過不代表你壞掉，只代表你也是人。
variations: 沒有人的人生是一次就過的，只是有些人剪掉了 NG。
你不是特別失敗，你只是剛好看得到自己的全部。

en.content:
You think you're the only one whose life is a mess.
The people you envy just don't post
the parts where they started over.
en.editorNote: For the night when it feels like everyone else got it together and you got left behind. You're seeing their highlight page, not their drafts. Falling apart doesn't make you broken — it makes you a person.
variations: Nobody gets it right on the first take. Some people just cut the outtakes.
You're not uniquely failing. You just happen to see all of your own footage.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'make friends with yourself, you'll never be alone' theme; reframed as the relationship you never break up with

zh-tw.content:
有一段關係，你這輩子都分不了手，
就是跟你自己的那段。
既然跑不掉，不如處得好一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給剛失戀、或很怕自己一個人的朋友。重點不是「不需要別人」，而是先把跟自己的關係經營好，剩下的關係才不會全押在別人身上。
variations: 別人可以離開你，你不行。所以對這個唯一的室友好一點。
跟自己合得來，走到哪都有伴。

en.content:
There's one relationship you can never break up with —
the one with yourself.
Since you're stuck together, you might as well get along.
en.editorNote: For a friend who just went through a breakup, or who's scared of being on their own. It's not that you don't need anyone — it's that once you're good company to yourself, you stop putting all of it on everyone else.
variations: Everyone else can walk out. You can't. So be kind to your only permanent roommate.
Get along with yourself and you'll have company everywhere you go.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you did the best you could with the tools you had at the time'; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
當時的你，只有當時的地圖。
別拿現在才學會的路，
去罵那個還在迷路的自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一直在為某個舊決定懊悔的人。你會後悔，正是因為你長大了、看得更遠了——那不是證明你當時很笨，是證明你現在更好了。放過以前的自己吧。
variations: 以前的你要是什麼都懂，就不叫「以前」了。
你已經為那件事道歉夠多次了，這次換成謝謝自己撐過來。

en.content:
Back then, you only had back-then's map.
Don't use the roads you learned later
to scold the you who was still lost.
en.editorNote: For anyone stuck replaying an old decision. The fact that you regret it means you grew and can see further now — that's proof you're better today, not proof you were stupid then. Let your past self off the hook.
variations: If past-you had known everything, it wouldn't be the past.
You've apologized to yourself enough. Try thanking yourself for making it through instead.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on permission to change your mind as an act of self-respect

zh-tw.content:
你有權改變主意。
昨天說好，今天想收回，
不叫善變，叫你更了解自己了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種答應了才後悔、卻硬著頭皮做下去的人。改變主意不是失信，是你拿到新資訊、聽見自己真正的感受後，願意重新選一次。這也是愛自己。
variations: 答應之前的你不是你，答應之後才更懂自己的你也是你。
反悔不用附上一篇檢討報告，一句「我改變心意了」就夠了。

en.content:
You're allowed to change your mind.
Saying yes yesterday and taking it back today
isn't being flaky — it's knowing yourself better.
en.editorNote: For the person who regrets saying yes but grinds through it anyway. Changing your mind isn't breaking your word; it's choosing again once you have new information and hear how you actually feel. That counts as self-love too.
variations: The you before you agreed and the you who knows better after are both you.
You don't owe a full report to change your mind. 'I've changed my mind' is a complete sentence.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on being proud of yourself without waiting for external praise

zh-tw.content:
不用等別人開口，
你也可以先為自己驕傲一次。
那些沒人看見的努力，你自己看見就夠了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合默默撐了很久、卻沒人拍拍肩膀的你。別再把「我很棒」的權利，交到別人手上。今天就練習對自己說一句：你做得很好，我看見了。
variations: 沒人幫你鼓掌，那就自己先拍一下。
你偷偷撐過的那些，值得你自己記一大功。

en.content:
You don't have to wait for someone else to say it —
you can be proud of yourself first.
The effort nobody saw, you saw. That's enough.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's been quietly holding it together with no one to pat them on the back. Stop handing the right to say 'I did good' to other people. Practice telling yourself today: you did well, and I noticed.
variations: If no one's clapping for you, start the applause yourself.
All the things you got through quietly deserve your own full credit.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on forgiving the past self who was in survival mode with limited tools

zh-tw.content:
別再罵那個過去的你了。
他當時手上只有那些工具，
已經盡力把你帶到今天了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜突然想起某個尷尬決定、羞恥到想鑽地洞的你。過去的你不是笨，只是還沒學到你現在會的事。試著在心裡跟他說一聲：辛苦了，謝謝你撐過來。
variations: 當時的你，是用當時懂的東西在做決定的，這樣就夠了。
你不是原諒錯誤，你是謝謝那個在暴風雨裡還沒放手的自己。

en.content:
Stop scolding the past version of you.
Back then he only had those tools,
and he still got you all the way to today.
en.editorNote: For the you who suddenly remembers some cringey decision at 2 a.m. and wants to disappear. Past-you wasn't dumb — he just hadn't learned what you know now. Try telling him: that was hard, thank you for getting through it.
variations: You made that call with what you understood at the time. That's enough.
You're not forgiving a mistake — you're thanking the you who didn't let go in the storm.

items.sourceNote: Body-neutrality angle: thanking the body for its function rather than judging its looks

zh-tw.content:
你的身體不是拿來被打分數的。
它今天幫你走了路、消化了飯、讓你好好呼吸——
光是這樣，就值得你說聲謝謝，而不是嫌棄。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合又在鏡子前挑自己毛病、或滑完健身帳號覺得自己不夠好的時候。先別急著喜歡它的樣子，光是感謝它一直在幫你運作，就已經是一種溫柔。今天洗澡時，試著跟身體說一句謝謝。
variations: 你的身體不是展示品，是每天默默載你到處跑的夥伴。
先謝謝它能動，再來慢慢學著喜歡它的樣子。

en.content:
Your body isn't here to be graded.
Today it walked you around, digested your food, kept you breathing —
that alone deserves a thank-you, not a complaint.
en.editorNote: For when you're picking yourself apart in the mirror, or feeling not-enough after scrolling fitness accounts. You don't have to love how it looks yet — just being grateful it keeps running for you is already a kind of gentleness. Try thanking your body in the shower tonight.
variations: Your body isn't a display piece — it's the partner quietly hauling you everywhere.
Thank it for working first. Learn to like how it looks later.

items.sourceNote: Original angle on not auditioning for people's approval to prove your worth

zh-tw.content:
別再為那些不打算選你的人試鏡了。
你的價值，不需要通過誰的甄選才算數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一直在某段關係或某個群體裡拚命表現、想被接受的你。你不是不夠好，是站錯了舞台。省下那些用力，留給真心想要你的人和地方。
variations: 他沒選你，不代表你不好，只代表你們不是同一齣戲的。
不用一直遞履歷給不想錄取你的人。

en.content:
Stop auditioning for people who were never going to cast you.
Your worth doesn't need to pass anyone's tryout to count.
en.editorNote: For the you who keeps performing in some relationship or group, hoping to finally be accepted. You're not not-enough — you're just on the wrong stage. Save that effort for the people and places that actually want you.
variations: Them not picking you doesn't mean you're bad — just that you're not in the same play.
Stop handing your résumé to people who were never going to hire you.

items.sourceNote: Self-abandonment angle: not shrinking yourself to soothe others' discomfort; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
別人不開心的時候，你不必急著把自己縮小去哄。
讓他去感受他的情緒，你留在自己這邊——這不是冷血，是不再拋下自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種一看到別人臉色不對，就馬上道歉、退讓、把想講的話吞回去的你。別人的情緒是他自己的功課，不是你要立刻擺平的責任。你可以體貼，但不用每次都拿自己去換對方的舒服。
variations: 他的難過不是你的錯，你不用馬上把自己折起來去接。
體貼別人跟拋棄自己，是兩件不一樣的事。

en.content:
When someone's upset, you don't have to shrink yourself to smooth it over.
Let them feel what they feel — and stay on your own side. That's not cold; it's just no longer abandoning yourself.
en.editorNote: For the you who apologizes, backs down, and swallows what you meant to say the second someone's face shifts. Their feelings are their own work, not an emergency you have to defuse. You can be kind without trading yourself for their comfort every time.
variations: Their sadness isn't your fault — you don't have to fold yourself up to catch it.
Being considerate and abandoning yourself are two different things.

items.sourceNote: Learning to receive angle: accepting help and compliments as self-love; original framing

zh-tw.content:
你很會給別人愛、給別人幫忙，
輪到別人對你好時，卻急著說「不用啦、我可以」。
學著把手張開收下——這也是愛自己的一種。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種嘴上很硬、什麼都自己扛、別人一要幫忙就渾身不自在的你。收下別人的好意不是欠人情，是給關係一個來回的機會。下次有人稱讚你或想幫你，試著只回一句「謝謝」，別急著否認。
variations: 別人誇你的時候，先接住，別急著說「沒有啦」。
你值得被好好對待，收下這件事不用覺得不好意思。

en.content:
You're so good at giving love and lending a hand,
but the second someone's good to you, you rush to say 'no need, I've got it.'
Learn to open your hands and receive — that's a form of self-love too.
en.editorNote: For the you who insists on carrying everything alone and squirms when anyone offers to help. Accepting kindness isn't racking up a debt — it lets the relationship flow both ways. Next time someone compliments you or offers help, just say 'thank you' instead of deflecting.
variations: When someone compliments you, catch it — don't rush to say 'oh, it's nothing.'
You deserve to be treated well. Receiving it doesn't have to feel awkward.

items.sourceNote: Self-blame reflex angle: not casting yourself as the problem in every conflict; original framing

zh-tw.content:
事情一出錯，你的第一個念頭永遠是「是不是我的問題」。
不是每件事都要你來扛——
有時候只是剛好不順，跟你夠不夠好無關。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種一有摩擦就先檢討自己、把所有問題都往身上攬的你。反射性地認錯不會讓你變好，只會讓你越縮越小。下次自責之前，先分清楚：這真的是我的錯，還是我只是習慣先怪自己？
variations: 不是每一段關係出問題，都是你不好。
先別急著認罪，這場你不一定是被告。

en.content:
The moment something goes wrong, your first thought is always 'was it me?'
Not everything is yours to answer for —
sometimes things just don't go smoothly, and it has nothing to do with whether you're good enough.
en.editorNote: For the you who audits yourself the instant there's friction and shoulders every problem in the room. Reflexively pleading guilty doesn't make you better — it just makes you smaller. Before the self-blame kicks in, sort it out: is this actually my fault, or am I just used to blaming myself first?
variations: Not every relationship that goes sideways is proof you're the problem.
Don't rush to plead guilty — you're not always the defendant here.

items.sourceNote: Summer 2026 wellness angle: bodies are for living in, not for qualifying for the season; original framing

zh-tw.content:
海不會先量你的腰圍才讓你下水。
夏天是拿來玩的，不是拿來被打分數的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合每年夏天都在心裡跟自己說「再瘦五公斤就去海邊」的你。真的去看看，海邊玩得最開心的那些人，沒有一個是先通過審核才下水的。收到朋友傳來的海邊邀約時，也可以直接轉傳這句給還在猶豫的他。
variations: 不用先變成「可以穿泳衣的身材」，你現在這副身體就已經可以下水了。
今年夏天的目標不是變好看，是玩得夠開心。

en.content:
The ocean doesn't check your measurements before it lets you in.
Summer is for playing, not for being graded.
en.editorNote: For the you who says 'five more pounds and then I'll go to the beach' every single summer. Look around next time — nobody having a great day in the water passed an inspection first. Also good to forward to the friend still hesitating over a beach invite.
variations: You don't need a 'swimsuit body.' You need a body, and you have one.
This summer's goal isn't looking good. It's having a good time.

items.sourceNote: 2026 self-trust angle: seeking external permission for a decision you've already made; original framing

zh-tw.content:
你已經問了一輪朋友，答案卻沒有比較清楚。
因為你早就知道要怎麼做了，
你只是在等一個人簽名——那個人是你自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種一有決定就開群組投票、問到第八個人還是睡不著的你。別人給的是他們的人生經驗，不是你的答案。下次問之前先寫下自己的第一直覺，你會發現後面問的都只是在找認同。
variations: 問到第十個人還是沒答案，因為缺的不是意見，是你自己的允許。
你需要的不是更多建議，是相信第一個浮出來的那個念頭。

en.content:
You've polled every friend you have and it's still not clearer.
Because you already know what you want to do —
you're just waiting for one person to sign off. That person is you.
en.editorNote: For the you who puts every decision to a group chat and is still awake after the eighth opinion. What people give you is their experience, not your answer. Next time, write down your first instinct before you ask anyone — you'll notice the rest was just hunting for permission.
variations: Ten opinions in and still stuck? You don't need advice. You need your own go-ahead.
Trust the thought that showed up first. It's usually the honest one.

items.sourceNote: Preventative self-care angle: small unglamorous admin as an act of love toward your future self; original framing

zh-tw.content:
愛自己有時候一點都不美，
就是把拖了三個月的看牙預約打完那通電話。
未來的你會很感謝現在的你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種待辦清單上永遠有一件小事沒處理、想到就胃緊一下的你。真正照顧自己的，往往不是點蠟燭泡澡，是替未來的自己拆掉一顆定時炸彈。今天挑一件最小的，做完就好。
variations: 把那件你一直逃避的小事做掉，比買十罐精油有用。
未來的你也是你，別老是把爛攤子留給他。

en.content:
Sometimes self-love isn't pretty at all.
It's finally making the dentist appointment you've dodged for three months.
Future you will be so grateful.
en.editorNote: For the you with one small task that's been on the list forever and tightens your stomach every time you see it. Real care is less candles-and-bath-bomb and more defusing a small bomb for the person you'll be next month. Pick the smallest one today and just finish it.
variations: Doing the one thing you keep avoiding beats ten bottles of fancy oil.
Future you is still you. Stop leaving them the mess.

items.sourceNote: 2026 slow-tech / digital burnout angle: you're not on call 24 hours; original framing

zh-tw.content:
手機靜音一個下午，世界不會塌。
你不是誰的二十四小時客服，
晚幾個小時回訊息，你還是一個好人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種訊息一跳出來就心跳加速、深怕別人覺得自己不理人的你。試試看週末挑一個下午把通知關掉，做點沒有生產力的事。真正在乎你的人，不會因為等了三小時就把你退貨。
variations: 已讀不回幾個小時，不會讓你變成壞人。
你可以隨時被找到，不代表你必須隨時被找到。

en.content:
Put your phone on silent for an afternoon. The world holds.
You're not anyone's 24-hour help desk —
replying a few hours late doesn't make you a bad person.
en.editorNote: For the you whose heart rate spikes at every notification, terrified of seeming like you're ignoring someone. Try one afternoon this weekend with notifications off, doing something with no output. Anyone who actually cares about you isn't returning you over a three-hour wait.
variations: Leaving a message unanswered for a few hours does not make you the villain.
Being reachable all the time doesn't mean you have to be.

items.sourceNote: Anti-commodified self-care angle: self-love isn't a purchase; original framing

zh-tw.content:
沒有人規定愛自己要花錢。
不用辦健身房會員、不用買香氛、不用報名療癒課程。
免費的那個版本叫做：
這次你說「我不想去」，然後真的沒去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看完一堆自我照顧貼文，反而覺得自己連愛自己都做不好的你。市面上賣的是「有在愛自己的樣子」，不是愛自己本身。真正有效的那些通常不用付費：說不、早點離場、不解釋。
variations: 愛自己不是一種消費，是一種選邊站。
最省錢的自我照顧：把「好啊」改成「這次我先不了」。

en.content:
Nobody said self-love has to cost money.
No gym membership, no diffuser, no healing workshop required.
The free version is this:
you said 'I don't want to go' — and then you didn't go.
en.editorNote: For the you who reads a hundred self-care posts and comes away feeling bad at self-care too. What's being sold is the look of loving yourself, not the thing itself. The versions that actually work are usually free: saying no, leaving early, not explaining.
variations: Self-love isn't a purchase. It's picking a side, and picking yours.
Cheapest self-care there is: swapping 'sure' for 'I'll sit this one out.'

items.sourceNote: Louise Hay 'you've criticized yourself for years and it hasn't worked' angle, reframed as an uninvited inner-critic committee; original metaphor

zh-tw.content:
你腦中那個一天到晚挑你毛病的聲音，
不是你花錢請來的顧問。
它從來沒繳出成績，你隨時可以請它閉嘴。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種腦內有個廣播電台、整天播放「你不夠好」的你。那個聲音講得很有自信，但翻翻它的履歷——它罵了你這麼多年，你有變更好嗎？下次它又開麥，你可以回一句：「這位不是我請的，散會。」
variations: 那個一直批評你的聲音，你沒投票選它上台。
你腦中的酸民，你不用付他薪水，也不用陪他開會。

en.content:
That voice in your head, the one nitpicking you all day —
you never hired it as a consultant.
It has no track record, and you can tell it to sit down anytime.
en.editorNote: For the you whose head runs a 24-hour station playing 'you're not good enough.' The voice sounds confident, but check its résumé — it's been criticizing you for years; did it ever make you better? Next time it grabs the mic, you can say: 'Nobody appointed you. Meeting adjourned.'
variations: You never voted that critical voice into office.
The heckler in your head isn't on payroll. You don't owe it a seat at the table.

items.sourceNote: Anti-toxic-positivity self-compassion angle (self-love includes letting yourself cry); original framing

zh-tw.content:
愛自己不是每天逼自己笑著說「都會好的」。
有時候是允許自己難過一場，
哭到夠了，再慢慢站起來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給對「保持正能量」有點過敏的你。硬撐出來的樂觀，其實只是把情緒往下壓，壓久了會反彈。真正的溫柔，是讓自己有難過的權利——不用馬上振作，也不用先解釋為什麼。感覺完了，力氣才會慢慢回來。
variations: 你不用一直很好，才算愛自己。難過的時候陪著自己，也算。
允許自己爛一天，不是放棄，是在充電。

en.content:
Loving yourself isn't forcing a smile and 'it'll all be fine' every day.
Sometimes it's letting yourself fall apart a little,
crying till you're done, then standing up slowly.
en.editorNote: For the you who's a little allergic to 'stay positive.' Forced optimism just presses the feelings down, and pressed-down things bounce back. Real tenderness is giving yourself the right to be sad — no bouncing back on cue, no explaining why first. Once you've felt it through, the energy comes back on its own.
variations: You don't have to be okay all the time to be loving yourself. Sitting with the sad counts too.
Letting yourself have a bad day isn't giving up. It's recharging.

items.sourceNote: Self-love as permission to outgrow relationships (growing apart isn't betrayal); original framing

zh-tw.content:
你可以長大到跟某些人走散。
那不是誰背叛了誰，
只是你們剛好長到了不同的方向。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種明明和某個朋友已經聊不太起來、卻還捨不得、覺得自己很無情的你。關係會過期，不代表當初是假的。人會長、路會分岔，放手讓彼此往各自的方向去，也是一種善良——對他，也對你自己。
variations: 有些人只陪你走一段，時間到了說聲謝謝就好，不用硬留。
你變了，這不是背叛，這叫成長。

en.content:
You're allowed to grow until you've drifted from certain people.
Nobody betrayed anybody —
you just happened to grow in different directions.
en.editorNote: For the you who can't quite talk to an old friend anymore but feels heartless for letting go. A relationship expiring doesn't mean it was ever fake. People grow, roads fork, and letting each other head your separate ways is its own kind of kindness — to them, and to you.
variations: Some people are only meant to walk part of the way. When it's time, just say thanks — you don't have to force them to stay.
You changed. That's not betrayal. That's growth.

items.sourceNote: 'You're not too much' angle — having needs isn't being difficult; original framing

zh-tw.content:
開口要你需要的東西，不叫難搞。
會餓、會累、需要被在乎，
這些都不是缺點，是你是個人的證明。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種每次想提出需求、話到嘴邊又吞回去、怕自己「太over」的你。有需要不是麻煩，是正常。把需求講清楚，別人才有機會好好對你——一直把自己調成靜音，只會累了自己，也讓在乎你的人猜不透。
variations: 你不是要求太多，你只是終於敢說出口了。
有需要不是任性，是誠實。

en.content:
Asking for what you need doesn't make you difficult.
Getting hungry, getting tired, wanting to be cared about —
none of it is a flaw. It's proof you're a person.
en.editorNote: For the you who swallows a request right as it reaches your lips, scared of being 'too much.' Having needs isn't a burden; it's normal. Spelling them out is what gives people a chance to treat you well — keeping yourself permanently on mute just wears you out and leaves the people who care guessing.
variations: You're not asking for too much. You just finally dared to say it out loud.
Having needs isn't being high-maintenance. It's being honest.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you are allowed to take up space' affirmation; rephrased with fresh framing

zh-tw.content:
你有資格佔一點空間。
不用縮著肩膀、壓低聲音、把自己折成別人方便的形狀。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種在群體裡總是自動退到角落、怕自己太顯眼的你。存在本來就會佔位置，那不是打擾，是理所當然。適合當作出門前的一句打氣。
variations: 不用一直道歉自己的存在。
你不是來當背景的。

en.content:
You're allowed to take up space.
No need to hunch your shoulders, lower your voice, or fold yourself into whatever shape is convenient for other people.
en.editorNote: For the you who always drifts to the corner of the room, scared of being too visible. Existing takes up room — that's not an intrusion, it's a given. Good as a pep line before you walk out the door.
variations: Stop apologizing for existing.
You didn't come here to be the background.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'your worth was never up for a vote' affirmation; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你的價值不用開放投票。
別人按不按讚，都不會改變你原本值多少。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合最近很在意數字、已讀、別人反應的你。價值不是民調，不會因為誰沒鼓掌就縮水。貼在限動當每週提醒也很好。
variations: 沒人按讚，你也還是原價。
你的價值不接受議價。

en.content:
Your worth was never up for a vote.
Whether people like it or not doesn't change what you're already worth.
en.editorNote: For when you've been fixating on numbers, read receipts, other people's reactions. Worth isn't a poll — it doesn't shrink because nobody clapped. Works as a weekly reset on your Stories.
variations: No likes? Still full price.
Your worth isn't open to negotiation.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you are not behind, you are becoming' caption; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
你不是落後了，
你只是還在長成自己的路上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種一打開社群就覺得別人都跑很前面、只有自己還在原地的你。人生不是同一條跑道，各自的花期本來就不一樣。適合在焦慮比較的深夜傳給自己。
variations: 沒有遲到這回事，你只是照自己的時區在走。
別人開花的時候，你可能正在紮根。

en.content:
You're not behind.
You're still becoming.
en.editorNote: For when you open social media and everyone seems miles ahead while you're standing still. Life isn't one shared track — everyone blooms on a different schedule. Good to send yourself on an anxious, comparison-heavy night.
variations: There's no such thing as late. You're just on your own timezone.
While others are blooming, you might be busy putting down roots.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'healing looks good on me' caption; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
好起來的樣子，很適合你。
你不用先變得完美，才有資格對自己好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給正在慢慢走出低潮的你。療癒不是一夕之間，是一天比一天多接住自己一點。適合當作復原期的自我肯定，或傳給正在努力好起來的朋友。
variations: 你正在好起來，這件事本身就很美。
慢慢來也是一種前進。

en.content:
Healing looks good on you.
You don't have to be perfect first to earn a little kindness from yourself.
en.editorNote: For the you who's slowly climbing out of a low patch. Healing isn't overnight — it's catching yourself a little better each day. Good as a recovery-season affirmation, or to send a friend who's working on getting better.
variations: You're getting better, and that alone is beautiful.
Going slow is still going forward.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by psychological-boundary framing (returning others' emotions); rephrased

zh-tw.content:
別人的情緒，記得還給別人。
你可以在乎，但不用整包扛回家。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種很容易被別人壞心情影響一整天、覺得都是自己的錯的你。同理不等於扛責，界線越清楚，心裡越穩。適合傳給心軟又容易內耗的朋友。
variations: 他的情緒是他的功課，不是你的作業。
你可以遞面紙，但不用連他的雨一起淋。

en.content:
Other people's emotions? Hand them back.
You can care without carrying the whole thing home.
en.editorNote: For the you whose whole day gets hijacked by someone else's bad mood, and who assumes it must be your fault. Empathy isn't the same as taking the blame — the clearer your boundary, the steadier you feel. Good to send a soft-hearted friend who burns out from overthinking.
variations: His mood is his homework, not your assignment.
You can pass the tissue without standing in his rain.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'muting, unfollowing is self-care' framing; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
退追那些讓你越滑越討厭自己的帳號，
不是玻璃心，是幫自己把心情擋在門外。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種每次滑完限動就莫名心情低落、開始嫌棄自己的你。你有權決定什麼進得了你的眼睛。按下靜音不是輸，是保養。適合在又被某個帳號戳到之後傳給自己。
variations: 會讓你變小的東西，本來就不該天天餵給自己看。
靜音一個帳號，比說服自己「不要在意」容易多了。

en.content:
Unfollow the accounts that make you like yourself less with every scroll.
That's not being fragile — it's keeping the mood out at the door.
en.editorNote: For the you whose whole mood dips after scrolling stories, then starts nitpicking yourself. You get to decide what makes it past your own eyes. Hitting mute isn't losing — it's maintenance. Good to send yourself right after some account pokes a sore spot.
variations: If it shrinks you, you don't owe it a daily seat in your feed.
Muting one account is a lot easier than convincing yourself not to care.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion 'celebrate small steps' framing; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
今天有回那封拖很久的訊息、有好好吃飯、有把自己撐到現在，
這些小事都值得你替自己拍拍手。
別總是等做出大事才肯給自己一句好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種只有考第一、升職、達標才覺得自己有價值的你。長期只盯著大目標，會忘記日子是靠一堆小小的努力撐起來的。適合在一個平凡但你有好好活過的日子，睡前對自己說。
variations: 小小的一步也是一步，值得替自己記一筆。
別人不一定看得到的努力，你自己要先看見、先鼓掌。

en.content:
You answered the message you'd been dreading, ate a real meal, kept yourself going until now.
Those small things are worth a little clap for yourself.
Stop waiting on something huge before you'll say one kind word.
en.editorNote: For the you who only feels worth something after acing the test, the promotion, the target hit. Staring only at the big goals, you forget the day is held up by a pile of tiny efforts. Good to tell yourself at bedtime on an ordinary day you actually lived well.
variations: A small step is still a step — log it in your own favor.
The effort no one else sees, you clap for first.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion 'inner dialogue' framing; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
別再拿自己開玩笑逗大家笑了。
那些「我就爛」「我最沒用」講久了，
連你自己都會開始當真。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種習慣先自嘲、把自己講得很糟來炒熱氣氛的你。玩笑話會偷偷變成你對自己的定義。要笑可以，但不用每次都拿自己當祭品。適合傳給那個很會逗別人、卻很兇對自己的朋友。
variations: 拿自己當笑點沒關係，但別把那句話留在心裡當真理。
你可以幽默，但不用每次都踩自己一腳。

en.content:
Stop making yourself the punchline just to get a laugh.
Say 'I'm useless,' 'I'm the worst' often enough
and even you start to believe it.
en.editorNote: For the you who reflexively self-deprecates to warm up the room. The joke quietly turns into how you define yourself. Laugh all you want, just stop offering yourself up as the sacrifice every time. Good to send the friend who's hilarious with everyone but brutal on themselves.
variations: Be the joke if you must, but don't keep that line as your truth.
You can be funny without stepping on yourself to do it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'befriending yourself / you deserve it now' framing; rephrased

zh-tw.content:
那件捨不得穿的好衣服、那瓶留著的香氛，別再等特別的日子了。
你不用先變成更好的自己，才配得上對自己好。
今天就是那個特別的日子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種好東西總是收著、覺得「等我瘦下來」「等我更成功」再享受的你。你一直在把自己的好日子往後延。其實你現在就值得。適合在你又想把某樣喜歡的東西收回櫃子時提醒自己。
variations: 留給「更好的自己」的那些好東西，現在的你就有資格用。
別再等以後了，你現在這個版本就值得被好好對待。

en.content:
That nice outfit you keep saving, that perfume you're hoarding — stop waiting for a special day.
You don't have to become a better you first to deserve good things.
Today is the special day.
en.editorNote: For the you who keeps the good stuff tucked away, saving it for 'once I lose the weight' or 'once I make it.' You keep postponing your own good days. You already deserve them now. Good to catch yourself with, right as you're about to put something you love back in the drawer.
variations: The good things you're saving for a 'better you' — the current you is allowed to use them.
Stop waiting for later. This version of you already deserves to be treated well.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 discourse on AI anxiety and re-defining human worth beyond output; fully rewritten

zh-tw.content:
現在寫字、畫圖、想點子，都有東西比你快、比你便宜。
但沒有任何一個模型，活過你活過的那些日子。
你的價值從來不在輸出速度，在你怎麼把日子過成你的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你看完一輪 AI 相關新聞、開始懷疑自己有沒有用的深夜。焦慮的來源通常不是技術，是你偷偷把「產出效率」當成自己值不值錢的標準。存起來，下次又比較的時候拿出來看。
variations: 比你快的東西每年都會出現，比你更像你的，一個都不會有。
把「我有沒有用」換成「我想怎麼過」，問題就不那麼可怕了。

en.content:
Writing, drawing, coming up with ideas — there's now something faster and cheaper than you at all of it.
But no model has lived a single one of your days.
Your worth was never about output speed. It's about how you make a life that's yours.
en.editorNote: For the late night after you've scrolled one too many AI headlines and started quietly wondering if you still count. The anxiety usually isn't about the technology — it's that you've been using output as the price tag on yourself. Save this for the next time you catch yourself doing it.
variations: Something faster than you shows up every year. Something more like you never will.
Swap 'am I still useful' for 'how do I want to live' and the question stops being scary.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 wellness-trend commentary on optimization fatigue and self-care becoming performance; rewritten

zh-tw.content:
喝水要記錄、睡覺有分數、冥想斷了連續紀錄還要補。
你的自我照顧，什麼時候變成第二份工作了？
愛自己不用打卡，做不到的那天也不用補交。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種把健康習慣做成一整排 app、然後因為連續紀錄斷掉而心情低落的人。當照顧自己也要考績，那就不是照顧了。適合在你看到某個 app 提醒跳出來、心裡先嘆一口氣的時候。
variations: 斷掉的連續紀錄不是失敗，只是你那天先照顧了更重要的事。
把追蹤自己的那些數字關掉一天，看看你身體自己怎麼說。

en.content:
Water logged, sleep scored, meditation streak to make up if you miss a day.
When did taking care of yourself turn into a second job?
Self-love doesn't need a streak, and there's nothing to make up on the days you skip.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose healthy habits have become a wall of apps, and who genuinely feels worse when a streak breaks. The moment caring for yourself gets a performance review, it stops being care. Good to read right as an app notification makes you sigh.
variations: A broken streak isn't failure. It just means something more human came first that day.
Turn the tracking off for one day and see what your body says on its own.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by body-neutrality discussion on deleting one's own photos; original framing and wording

zh-tw.content:
那些被你刪掉的照片裡，有很多是你笑得最開心的樣子。
你只是不喜歡那天的臉，
卻連那天的快樂一起丟掉了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種每次朋友傳合照來，第一件事是放大自己的臉、然後說「這張不要」的人。你保留下來的回憶，正在被一個很嚴格的審查員一張張刷掉。下次手指移到刪除之前，先看看照片裡發生了什麼事。
variations: 先看照片裡那天發生了什麼，再決定要不要刪。
你不是在刪一張醜照，你是在刪一段你在場的證據。

en.content:
A lot of the photos you deleted are the ones where you're laughing hardest.
You didn't like your face that day,
so you threw out the whole day with it.
en.editorNote: For the person who zooms straight in on their own face whenever a friend sends a group photo, then says 'delete that one.' A very strict editor is quietly culling your memories. Next time your finger hovers over delete, look at what was actually happening in the picture.
variations: Look at what that day was before you decide whether to delete it.
You're not deleting a bad photo. You're deleting proof you were there.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by people-pleasing / over-apologizing communication patterns; original scenario and wording

zh-tw.content:
那則訊息你改了五次才敢按送出，對方三個字就回完了。
不是你想太多有問題，
是你太怕自己會變成別人的麻煩。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種傳個訊息要先打草稿、刪掉一堆「不好意思」再重打的人。你花在斟酌的力氣，比事情本身還多。適合在你又對著輸入框發呆五分鐘的時候看一眼——你開口本來就不需要那麼多資格審查。
variations: 你不用把每句話都磨到不會冒犯任何人，才有資格開口。
你怕麻煩到別人的程度，已經先麻煩到你自己了。

en.content:
You rewrote that message five times before hitting send. They replied with three words.
The problem isn't that you overthink.
It's how scared you are of being someone's inconvenience.
en.editorNote: For the person who drafts a text, deletes four apologies, and starts over. You spend more energy wording it than the thing itself is worth. Read this the next time you've been staring at the message box for five minutes — speaking up doesn't require that much clearance.
variations: You don't have to sand every sentence down to something that can't bother anyone.
How hard you try not to be a burden has already become a burden on you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 'quiet burnout' and preventative-rest commentary; rewritten with original framing

zh-tw.content:
「等這個案子結束就好好休息。」
上一個案子結束的時候，你也是這樣說的。
休息不是忙完的獎品，是你要先排進去的行程。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種永遠有下一個「忙完再說」的人。忙完的那天不會自己到，它只會被下一件事接手。適合在你又要把休假往後挪的那天看——先把日子圈起來，再去排別的。
variations: 把休息排進行事曆，不是等有空才補上。
你已經延了三次的那個假，其實一次都沒有真的比較不方便。

en.content:
"I'll rest properly once this project wraps."
You said the exact same thing when the last one wrapped.
Rest isn't the prize for finishing. It's the thing you book first.
en.editorNote: For anyone who always has one more 'after this' waiting. That free stretch never arrives on its own — the next thing just takes its slot. Read this on the day you're about to push your time off back again. Block the days first, then schedule around them.
variations: Put rest on the calendar instead of waiting for a gap to appear.
That break you've postponed three times was never actually less convenient the first time.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by counselling commentary on how chronic people-pleasing disconnects you from your own preferences; rewritten with original framing and examples

zh-tw.content:
「吃什麼？」「都可以。」
「哪天方便？」「你決定。」
讓久了，連你自己都不知道你想吃什麼了。
今天挑一件很小的事，把你真正想要的那個講出來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種揪吃飯永遠讓別人選、有意見也先嚥回去的人。不是要你突然變得很有主張，先從一杯飲料的甜度、一部想看的片開始就好。把偏好講出口，是在提醒自己：我也在這桌上。
variations: 先從「我想吃拉麵」這種小事開始練，你的喜好不用先徵求同意。
說出你想要的，不會讓你變難搞，只會讓你比較不像個布景。

en.content:
"Where should we eat?" "I'm easy."
"Which day works?" "You pick."
Say it long enough and you stop knowing what you actually wanted.
Pick one tiny thing today and say the real answer out loud.
en.editorNote: For the person who always lets someone else choose the restaurant and swallows their own opinion first. You don't have to turn into a diva overnight — start with the drink you want or the movie you'd actually pick. Naming a preference is how you remind yourself you're at the table too.
variations: Start small: "I want ramen." Your preferences don't need anyone's sign-off.
Saying what you want doesn't make you difficult. It makes you less like scenery.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by lifestyle reporting on post-work decompression habits; rewritten with an original scene and framing

zh-tw.content:
已經到家了，你還在樓下多坐五分鐘才上去。
那五分鐘不是在拖，
是你在把外面那個版本的自己，先好好收起來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給一進門就要立刻切換成爸媽、伴侶、室友、好脾氣的那種人。中間那個空檔不用偷偷來，也不用覺得抱歉——它讓你回家的時候，是你自己，不是還在加班的那個人。
variations: 在機車坐墊上多待的那幾分鐘，是今天唯一屬於你的行程。
進門前先吸一口氣，你不用一秒就變成另一個角色。

en.content:
You're already home, but you sit downstairs five more minutes before going up.
Those five minutes aren't stalling.
That's you putting away the version of yourself the day needed.
en.editorNote: For anyone who has to switch instantly into parent, partner, roommate, or nice-person mode the moment the door opens. That gap doesn't have to be sneaked, and it doesn't need an apology — it's what lets you walk in as yourself instead of as someone still at work.
variations: The extra few minutes sitting in the parked car are the only thing on today's calendar that's yours.
Take one breath before the door. You don't have to become someone else in a single second.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by reporting on negativity bias (it takes several compliments to offset one criticism); rewritten as an original bookkeeping metaphor, no clinical claims

zh-tw.content:
十句誇你的話，你一句都沒留下；
一句酸你的話，你背了三年。
不是你太敏感，是你記帳只記壞的那一筆。
今天補記一筆：那十句也是真的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種被誇就先幫對方補一句「他只是客套」、被念一句卻能反覆重播到半夜的人。你的腦本來就偏心壞消息，這不是你的個性有問題。適合在你又在心裡重播某句話的時候，翻出那十句一起算進去。
variations: 你的內心帳本漏記太多好事了，今天把它補齊。
壞的那句你記得住，好的那些也該有位子。

en.content:
Ten people told you that you did well and none of it stuck.
One person said you weren't enough and you've carried it for three years.
You're not too sensitive — you just only log the bad entries.
Add one today: those ten were true too.
en.editorNote: For the person who hears a compliment and immediately files it under "they were just being polite," then replays one offhand criticism until 2am. Your brain is wired to favour bad news — that's not a personality flaw. Next time a line is on loop, count the ten you skipped.
variations: Your inner ledger is missing a lot of good entries. Fill some in today.
If the harsh line gets to stay in your head, the kind ones should get a seat too.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion writing on validating your own experience instead of answering on auto-pilot; rewritten as an original everyday dialogue scene

zh-tw.content:
「你最近還好嗎？」
「還好啊。」
這兩個字你講得比誰都順，順到自己都沒認真想過答案。
今天換個人問——你自己問，然後老實回一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種被關心時反射性回「還好」的人。適合睡前傳給朋友，或在自己又用兩個字打發過去的那天，停下來真的問自己一次。
variations: 「還好」是你最常說的那句謊，而且只騙得過你自己。
別人問你好不好，你答得很快；輪到自己問自己，你反而卡住了。

en.content:
"How have you been?"
"Fine."
You say it so smoothly you never stop to check whether it's true.
Ask yourself today — and answer honestly for once.
en.editorNote: For the person whose reflex answer is always "fine." Send it to a friend before bed, or keep it for the day you catch yourself brushing off the question again.
variations: "Fine" is the lie you tell most often, and the only person it fools is you.
You answer that question fast for everyone else. Try answering it slowly for yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by body-neutral self-acceptance themes (accepting yourself as you are, not after changing); rewritten around an original clothing-size scene

zh-tw.content:
褲子拉不上來，是那條褲子的尺碼不對，
不是你這個人不對。
衣服本來就該來配合你的身體，
沒有人規定你要先變成一個衣架子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 換季翻出舊衣服、在試衣間被一個數字影響一整天心情的時候，先看這一句再決定要不要難過。
variations: 尺碼只是工廠設定的一個數字，不是你的成績單。
那件穿不下的衣服只證明它不適合你，不證明你哪裡有問題。

en.content:
If the jeans don't zip, the jeans are the wrong size — you aren't.
Clothes are supposed to fit your body, not the other way around.
Nobody signed you up to become a hanger first.
en.editorNote: For fitting-room days and end-of-season closet clean-outs, when one number on a tag threatens to run your whole mood.
variations: A size is a number a factory picked. It is not your report card.
The shirt that doesn't fit is information about the shirt.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 commentary on stepping back from productivity culture that ties worth to output; rewritten as an original piece about hobbies you never get good at

zh-tw.content:
你已經很久沒做那種「做了也不會變厲害」的事了。
亂彈一首彈不熟的曲子、把顏料塗得亂七八糟，
那兩個小時看起來什麼都沒換到，
但那是你還記得自己是誰的證據。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給把每個興趣都經營成副業、連放鬆都要有產出的人。這個週末挑一件永遠不會拿去換錢的喜歡，做得很爛也沒關係。
variations: 不是每件事都要進作品集，有些事做爽的就好。
你可以留一件永遠做不好、也永遠不變現的喜歡。

en.content:
It has been a long time since you did something you'll never get good at.
Fumbling through a song, making a mess with paint —
two hours that produced nothing you could show anyone.
That's not wasted time. That's you remembering who you are.
en.editorNote: For anyone who has turned every hobby into a side hustle. Pick one thing this weekend that will never be monetized, and be cheerfully bad at it.
variations: Not everything has to go in the portfolio. Some things are just for fun.
You're allowed one hobby you stay terrible at forever.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion material on validating your experience instead of minimizing it; rewritten as an original take on ranking your pain against other people's

zh-tw.content:
每次講到自己的難，你都要自動補一句：
「不過比起別人，我這根本沒什麼。」
難不是比賽，沒有人規定你要先贏過誰，才有資格喊累。
你的辛苦，維持原本的大小就可以。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那種抱怨到一半就開始替自己打折的人。適合在你又想說「我這樣算幸福了」的時候，把話停在真心話那一句。
variations: 你不用把自己的難，壓到別人剛好聽得下去的大小。
世界上永遠有人更辛苦，但那不會讓你現在比較不痛。

en.content:
Every time you mention something hard, you tack on the discount:
"But other people have it way worse, so it's really nothing."
Pain isn't a contest. You don't have to out-suffer anyone to be allowed to say you're tired.
Your hard thing gets to stay the size it actually is.
en.editorNote: For the friend who apologizes halfway through venting. Next time you reach for "I shouldn't complain," stop at the honest sentence instead.
variations: You don't have to shrink what's hard until it's easy for other people to hear.
Someone always has it worse. That has never once made your day hurt less.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 wellness coverage naming rest and recovery as non-negotiable rather than earned; rewritten as an original reframe of late-night scrolling

zh-tw.content:
你不是不想睡，
你只是整天都在忙別人的事，到了半夜才終於有一段時間是你的。
所以問題從來不是你太晚睡，
是你的一天裡，沒有一格是先留給自己的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給每天喊累、卻捨不得關手機的人。與其半夜硬補三小時，明天先在白天替自己卡一段三十分鐘。
variations: 熬夜滑手機不是自制力差，是你在把被拿走的一天要回來一點。
先在行事曆上留一格給自己，凌晨那三小時才捨得還給睡眠。

en.content:
It's not that you don't want to sleep.
You spent the whole day on everyone else, and midnight is the first slice of it that belongs to you.
The real problem was never your bedtime.
It's that nothing in your day was set aside for you first.
en.editorNote: For anyone exhausted at 1am and still scrolling. Instead of clawing back three hours at night, block thirty minutes for yourself tomorrow while it's still light out.
variations: Late-night scrolling isn't weak willpower. It's you taking back a day that got spent on other people.
Put one square on tomorrow's calendar that's yours, and midnight gets easier to give up.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 Taiwanese workplace-psychology commentary on emotional labour and holding a stable frame at work; rewritten as an original scene about being asked for a quick favour

zh-tw.content:
「這個你順手幫一下就好。」
那個「順手」，是別人替你的時間開的價。
你會的東西不是附贈的，
你可以幫，但要是你決定要幫，
而不是對方已經先幫你決定了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給那個總是被叫去「順便處理一下」的人。下次不用馬上答應也不用翻臉，先回一句「我看一下我的時間」，把決定權拿回自己手上。
variations: 別人說「很快啦」的時候，通常是他不用花那個時間。
你願意幫忙是好事，但那要是禮物，不是預設值。

en.content:
"Could you just quickly handle this for me?"
That word "quickly" is someone else pricing your time for you.
What you're good at isn't a free add-on.
You can say yes — but let it be you deciding,
not someone deciding on your behalf.
en.editorNote: For the person who always gets the "while you're at it" tasks. You don't have to snap or agree on the spot — "let me check my week" hands the decision back to you.
variations: When someone says it'll only take a second, notice whose second it is.
Helping is a gift you give. It stops being one when it's assumed.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by boundary-beginner material on people-pleasing as self-abandonment; rewritten around the compliment of having an easy temper

zh-tw.content:
「你脾氣真好，都不會生氣。」
聽起來像稱讚，
但其實只是每一次的不舒服，你都自己吞掉了。
生氣不代表你變壞了，
那是有一條線被踩到，心裡在提醒你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給常被說「好相處」的人。不用大吵，一句「這樣我有點不舒服」就夠了——講出來是為了讓關係走得長，不是為了贏。
variations: 被說「你都不會生氣」的時候，可以想一下：是真的不氣，還是不敢氣。
溫和是選擇，不是義務。你可以溫和，也可以有底線。

en.content:
"You're so easygoing, nothing ever bothers you."
It sounds like a compliment,
but it usually means you swallowed every time something did.
Anger doesn't make you a worse person.
It's a line getting crossed, and something in you saying so.
en.editorNote: For anyone known as the easy one. You don't need a fight — "that didn't sit right with me" is enough. Saying it keeps the relationship honest instead of quietly expensive.
variations: Next time you hear "you never get mad," ask whether you don't — or whether you don't dare.
Gentle is a choice, not a job description. You can be kind and still have a limit.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion writing on treating your own needs as legitimate; rewritten as an original August-heat scene about not spending on your own comfort

zh-tw.content:
家裡有客人你二話不說開冷氣，
只剩自己的時候，卻可以熱到滿身汗還撐著。
你不是在省電，
你是覺得自己不值得那幾十塊。
你的舒服不用先通過成本審查。
zh-tw.editorNote: 八月最熱的那幾天可以拿出來看看。今天挑一件你會替別人做、卻捨不得替自己做的小事，做給自己一次。
variations: 你替別人買的體貼，也記得留一份原價給自己。
願意讓自己舒服一點，不是浪費，是你把自己也算成了人。

en.content:
When someone's over, you turn the air conditioning on without thinking.
Alone, you'll sit and sweat through it.
You're not saving money.
You've decided you're not worth the couple of dollars.
Your comfort doesn't have to pass a cost review first.
en.editorNote: Worth rereading on the worst week of August. Pick one small thing you'd do for a guest without hesitating, and do it for yourself today.
variations: The care you hand out at full price, save a little of it for yourself.
Letting yourself be comfortable isn't waste. It's counting yourself as a person too.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 commentary pushing back on worth-as-output culture; rewritten as an original piece about a January goal list checked in August

zh-tw.content:
一月寫的那張清單，到現在只打勾兩項。
可是清單上沒寫的是：
你熬過了幾個爛掉的月份、陪一個人度過難關、
還把自己好好帶到了八月。
沒有打勾，不代表你這半年沒有在活。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在下半年開頭、翻到年初目標時看。與其重寫一張更長的清單，不如先寫下這半年真正發生過、但你沒記上去的三件事。
variations: 有些最重要的事，本來就不長成待辦事項的樣子。
你不是進度落後，你只是走了一條清單上沒畫的路。

en.content:
That list you wrote in January has two boxes ticked.
What the list doesn't show:
the months you got through, the person you sat with when it was bad,
and the fact that you got yourself all the way to August.
An unticked box doesn't mean you weren't living.
en.editorNote: Good for the start of the second half of the year, when your old goals resurface. Instead of writing a longer list, write down three real things from these months that never made it onto one.
variations: The things that mattered most rarely show up shaped like a to-do item.
You're not behind. You took a route the list never had on it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 therapist commentary on family-guilt phrases like 'family comes first'; rewritten as an original scene about the phrase used to end negotiations

zh-tw.content:
「一家人，幹嘛計較。」
這句話通常不是在講感情，
是在提醒你：這件事沒有商量空間。
你可以愛他們，也可以說「這次我沒辦法」。
界線不是不認人，是讓這段關係還撐得住。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被親近的人用「我們是一家人」帶過需求時。回覆時不用辯論那句話，只回你能做到的範圍：可以做什麼、不能做什麼、什麼時候有空。
variations: 感情不是免死金牌，關係再親，也還是有兩個人。
你不是在拒絕他們，你只是不想再從自己身上扣。

en.content:
"We're family — why are you keeping score?"
That line usually isn't about love.
It's a signal that the topic is closed.
You can love them and still say, "I can't do that this time."
A boundary isn't disowning anyone. It's what keeps you in the room.
en.editorNote: For when someone close ends a conversation with "but we're family." Don't argue with the line — answer with your actual range: what you can do, what you can't, and when.
variations: Being related doesn't make a request automatic.
You're not turning them down. You're done taking it out of your own account.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by CBT double-standard method coverage in 2026 self-compassion writing; rewritten as an original workplace scene about writing a self-review

zh-tw.content:
同事請你幫忙寫推薦語，你三分鐘寫滿一整段，句句是真的。
輪到自己那份自評，你在「還可以」四個字前面坐了一小時。
不是你沒有優點，
是你只對自己啟用最嚴格的那套標準。
那段誇同事的話，也照著寫給自己一次看看。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在寫自評、更新履歷或面試前看。可以直接做一次：把你會替最要好的同事寫的那段話抄下來，再把名字換成自己的。
variations: 你替別人找優點的眼力，其實一直都在，只是很少往內用。
同一件事，換成別人做你會說很厲害，換成你就叫「本來就該做到」。

en.content:
A coworker asks you for a recommendation blurb. You write a full paragraph in three minutes, all of it true.
Then you sit in front of your own self-review for an hour and type "fine."
It's not that you have nothing good to list.
It's that you only run the strict rubric on yourself.
Try writing that coworker's paragraph again, with your own name in it.
en.editorNote: Good before a self-review, a resume update, or an interview. Do it literally: write the blurb you'd write for your favorite coworker, then swap in your name.
variations: You've always had the eye for other people's strengths. You just rarely point it inward.
Same work: impressive when they do it, "the bare minimum" when you do.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 boundary-guilt writing on over-explaining after saying no; rewritten as an original scene about apologizing your way out of a decline

zh-tw.content:
你回絕了那場聚會，然後補了三段語音解釋，
最後還加一句「下次我請客」。
拒絕本身只花了兩秒，
後面那些是你在替一個不存在的罪付贖金。
「這次我不行」就是完整的句子，不用附帶利息。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在按下「不好意思我這次不去」之後、手指又想再補一句時看。練習：說完不行就把對話關掉，不追加解釋、不預支下一次的補償。
variations: 拒絕不用附理由，附了反而像在等對方批准。
你不欠他一份說明書，你只是那天不想去。

en.content:
You turned down the dinner, then sent three voice notes explaining,
and closed with "next one's on me."
The no took two seconds.
Everything after it was you paying bail for a crime you didn't commit.
"I can't this time" is a whole sentence. It doesn't accrue interest.
en.editorNote: For the moment right after you decline, when your thumb wants to add one more line. Practice: send the no, then close the app. No extra reasons, no prepaid make-up plans.
variations: A no with a paragraph attached starts sounding like a request for approval.
You don't owe anyone documentation. You just didn't want to go.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 CBT double-standard material on tolerating treatment you'd never accept for a friend; rewritten as an original scene about advice you give versus advice you take

zh-tw.content:
同樣一句話，朋友被這樣講，你立刻說：他憑什麼。
換成你被這樣講，你說：可能是我自己沒做好。
你替別人生氣的標準那麼清楚，
輪到自己就自動打折。
下次先問一句：如果今天是他，我會叫他忍嗎？
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在被主管、同事或家人講了難聽話、開始自我檢討時看。把當下那句話原封不動想像成是朋友被講的，你的反應就是答案。
variations: 你對別人的標準，通常才是那個公平的版本。
你不是太玻璃心，你只是終於用同一把尺量自己。

en.content:
Same sentence. Said to a friend, you're instantly indignant: who talks to people like that?
Said to you, it becomes: maybe I just didn't do a good enough job.
You know exactly where the line is when you're defending someone else.
Then you quietly discount it for yourself.
Next time, ask first: if this were them, would I tell them to let it go?
en.editorNote: For the moment a manager, coworker, or relative says something cutting and you start auditing yourself. Replay the exact sentence as if it landed on a friend — your reaction is the answer.
variations: The standard you hold for other people is usually the fair one.
You're not too sensitive. You just finally measured yourself with the same ruler.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 writing on guilt-driven people-pleasing; rewritten as an original scene about keeping an unwanted gift out of obligation

zh-tw.content:
那個你根本不喜歡的擺飾，在櫃子上放了四年，
只因為送的人偶爾會來。
你家的空間有限，
卻分了一格出去，用來保管別人的心情。
收下心意就夠了，東西可以走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在整理房間、卻在某個物品前卡住的時候看。判斷方式很簡單：留著它，是因為你喜歡，還是因為你怕被問？
variations: 感謝過了，就算收完了，剩下的處置權是你的。
你家不是別人心意的倉庫。

en.content:
That ornament you never liked has held a shelf for four years,
because the person who gave it to you visits sometimes.
Your space is finite,
and you've assigned a slot of it to storing someone else's feelings.
You can keep the gesture and let the object go.
en.editorNote: For when you're clearing out a room and freeze in front of one object. The test is simple: are you keeping it because you like it, or because you're afraid of being asked about it?
variations: You said thank you. That transaction is complete — what happens next is yours.
Your home isn't a storage unit for other people's good intentions.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 writing on quiet self-worth struggles and presenting an approved version of yourself; rewritten as an original scene about waiting until you're fine before letting anyone near

zh-tw.content:
你把難看的那幾天全部留在家裡，
等自己站穩了、講得出完整句子了，才敢出現在別人面前。
然後你說：怎麼都沒有人真的認識我。
他們認識的一直是那個修好之後的版本，
因為你只讓那個版本出門。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在婉拒了朋友的邀約、理由是「我最近狀態不好」的那個晚上看。不是要你把所有難堪攤開，只是挑一個人，試著在還沒好起來的時候就讓他看見一次。
variations: 你不用先痊癒，才有資格被陪。
只讓人看見完好的你，等於請他們去認識一個不存在的人。

en.content:
You keep the ugly days indoors,
and only step outside once you're steady and can finish a sentence again.
Then you wonder why nobody really knows you.
They've only ever met the repaired version,
because that's the only one you let out of the house.
en.editorNote: For the night you turn down an invitation with "I'm not in a great place right now." You don't have to hand anyone the whole mess. Just pick one person and let them see you before you're fixed, once.
variations: You don't have to finish healing to deserve company.
If people only meet the polished version, you've introduced them to someone who doesn't exist.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 material on why people can't celebrate their own wins; rewritten as an original scene about announcing your own good news as if it were an accident

zh-tw.content:
朋友考上的那天，你訂了蛋糕、寫了三百字。
輪到你自己有好消息，你打了一行「其實我上禮拜過了」，
還加了個「哈哈也沒什麼啦」。
你把自己的好事講得像不小心發生的，
好像高興太明顯就是一種冒犯。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你剛完成一件很久的事、卻不知道要不要說出口的時候看。今天挑一件小事，用你替朋友慶祝的那個力氣，替自己做一次——訂那個蛋糕也行。
variations: 你的好消息不需要先道歉再登場。
替自己開心不會佔到別人的份。

en.content:
When your friend got in, you ordered a cake and wrote three paragraphs.
When it was your turn, you typed "oh btw I passed last week,"
and tacked on "haha it's not a big deal."
You announce your own good news like it happened by accident,
as if being visibly happy would be rude.
en.editorNote: For right after you finish something you worked on for ages and can't decide whether to mention it. Pick one small thing today and spend on yourself the same energy you'd spend celebrating a friend. The cake counts.
variations: Your good news doesn't have to apologize before it walks in.
Being happy for yourself doesn't take anyone else's share.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 self-compassion writing on the inner critic pre-screening what you say; rewritten as an original scene about the message you type out and delete

zh-tw.content:
那段話你打了三次，改到很客氣，最後整段刪掉，
三分鐘後有人講了幾乎一樣的東西，大家說很有道理。
你的意見從來沒有被否決過，
因為它在送出之前就先被你自己攔下來了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在會議或群組裡默默清空輸入框之後看。下次先別評分，把那句話送出去，讓它自己去面對世界——被回應或被略過都可以，但至少它出過場。
variations: 你腦中那個審稿的人，從來沒有拿到過這個職位。
先送出去，再看結果，不要在自己這關就結案。

en.content:
You typed it three times, softened it, then deleted the whole thing.
Three minutes later someone said nearly the same thing and the room called it a good point.
Your opinion has never actually been rejected.
It keeps getting stopped by you, before it ever leaves the box.
en.editorNote: For the moment right after you quietly clear the text field in a meeting or a group chat. Next time, skip the grading and send it. It can get answered or ignored — at least it made it into the room.
variations: Nobody ever gave that editor in your head the job.
Send it first, judge it after. Don't close the case at your own desk.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 writing on worth contingent on output and ignoring your own limits; rewritten as an original scene about translating body signals into permission to keep going

zh-tw.content:
肩膀緊了兩個月，你說「大概是姿勢問題」。
胃怪怪的三個禮拜，你說「應該還好」。
你身體講的每一句話，都被你翻譯成「還可以撐」。
它不是在抱怨，它是在報告。
你至少可以聽完，再決定要不要繼續。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又把某個拖了很久的不舒服笑著帶過的時候看。今天做一件很小的事就好：把那個一直沒排的檢查、那個沒去的門診，先查一下時間。
variations: 身體不會誇大，它只是講了很多次都沒人回應。
把「還可以」換成「我聽到了」，就已經是一種照顧。

en.content:
Your shoulder's been tight for two months — probably just posture.
Your stomach's been off for three weeks — it's probably nothing.
Every sentence your body says, you translate as "can still keep going."
It isn't complaining. It's reporting.
You could at least hear it out before deciding.
en.editorNote: For when you've just laughed off a discomfort you've been carrying for months. One small thing today: look up the hours for the appointment you keep not making.
variations: Your body doesn't exaggerate. It just repeats itself until someone answers.
Swapping "I'm fine" for "I hear you" already counts as taking care of it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by therapist writing on over-apologizing as a learned survival habit; rewritten as an original scene about apologetic message openers

zh-tw.content:
「不好意思打擾一下」
「抱歉這麼晚傳訊息」
「不好意思又來麻煩你」
你每次開口之前，都先付一次過路費。
