可是你要講的那件事，本來就有資格佔別人三十秒。
下次試試看，第一句就直接講事情。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又把開頭那句道歉刪掉、然後又打回去的時候看。今天挑一則不重要的訊息，開場白直接寫要講的事。
variations: 「不好意思」留給你真的做錯的時候，其他時候，你只是在說話而已。
把「抱歉打擾」換成「想跟你確認一件事」，同一件事，你就不再是來討空間的人。

en.content:
"Sorry to bother you—"
"Sorry for messaging so late—"
"Sorry to be a pain again—"
You pay a toll before every sentence you send.
But the thing you need to say was always worth thirty seconds of someone's time.
Try it once: open with the actual sentence.
en.editorNote: For when you've deleted and retyped that opening apology three times. Pick one low-stakes message today and start it with the point instead.
variations: Save "sorry" for the times you actually got something wrong. The rest of the time, you're just talking.
Swap "sorry to bother you" for "quick question" — same message, and you stop asking permission to exist.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by therapist-approved tools for people-pleasers around naming your own needs; rewritten as an original scene about remembering everyone's food restrictions except your own

zh-tw.content:
你記得誰不吃牛、誰對堅果過敏、誰只喝去冰，
訂餐的時候一個都不會漏。
可是同一桌坐了三年，
沒有人知道你其實不吃香菜——
因為你每次都自己挑掉。
你的喜好不是麻煩，只是你從來沒講出口。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又默默把不喜歡的東西挑到碗邊的時候看。下一次點餐，把屬於你的那句備註也講出來，一句就好。
variations: 「我不吃這個」不是在刁難，是在讓人真的認識你。
你把所有人的口味都記起來了，總可以留一格給自己。

en.content:
You know who skips beef, who's allergic to nuts, who wants no ice —
you never miss one when you're ordering for the table.
But after three years at that same table,
nobody knows you don't eat cilantro,
because you just pick it out yourself every time.
Your preferences aren't an inconvenience. You've just never said them out loud.
en.editorNote: For when you've quietly pushed something you dislike to the edge of your plate again. Next time you order, say your one request out loud. Just the one.
variations: "I don't eat that" isn't being difficult. It's letting people actually meet you.
You've memorized everyone else's preferences. You can keep one slot for your own.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 material on people-pleasers avoiding minor conflict; rewritten as an original scene about accepting wrong orders rather than speaking up

zh-tw.content:
飲料做成全糖，你說沒關係；
送來的是別桌的餐，你吃了兩口就算了；
褲子改短了兩公分，你說這樣也能穿。
你不是好相處，
你只是覺得「講出來」比「吞下去」更麻煩。
「不好意思，這個跟我點的不一樣。」
這句話不會傷到任何人，包括你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又對著一個不對的東西說「沒關係」的時候看。下次遇到小小的出錯，練習把那句話講完，語氣可以很客氣，但要講。
variations: 客氣跟委屈是兩件事，你可以只留下前面那個。
願意開口更正，是你對自己最基本的一種尊重。

en.content:
The drink came full-sugar and you said it's fine.
Someone else's order landed on your table and you'd already had two bites, so never mind.
The hem got taken up two inches too short and you said you could still wear it.
You're not easygoing.
You've just decided that speaking up costs more than swallowing it.
"Sorry, this isn't what I ordered."
That sentence doesn't hurt anyone. Including you.
en.editorNote: For when you've said "it's fine" to something that wasn't. Next small mix-up, finish the sentence. Polite is allowed. Silent isn't required.
variations: Being gracious and being shortchanged are two different things. You only have to keep the first one.
Correcting something politely is the most basic respect you can show yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by psychology writing on applying gentler standards to others than to yourself; rewritten as an original scene about tolerating broken things only for yourself

zh-tw.content:
朋友說椅子會搖，你馬上回：換一張啊，坐起來不安全。
你自己那張搖了一年半，你說：習慣了，還能坐。
杯子裂了你繼續用，濾芯過期你說再撐一下。
你給別人的標準是「這樣不行」，
給自己的標準是「還沒完全壞」。
你也可以是那個值得換一張好椅子的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又對著一個該換的東西說「還能用」的時候看。今天挑最小的那一個：把每天都讓你不舒服的那樣東西換掉。
variations: 「還能用」跟「用起來舒服」，中間差的是你有沒有把自己算進去。
你不用等東西徹底壞掉，才准自己過得好一點。

en.content:
Your friend mentions a wobbly chair and you say: replace it, that's not safe to sit on.
Yours has wobbled for a year and a half and you say: I'm used to it, it still works.
The mug's cracked and you keep using it. The filter's expired and you say it can hold out a while longer.
Your standard for everyone else is "that's not okay."
Your standard for yourself is "not completely broken yet."
You're allowed to be someone who gets a chair that doesn't wobble.
en.editorNote: For when you've told yourself something still works when it clearly doesn't. Pick the smallest one today: replace the thing that annoys you every single morning.
variations: The gap between "still usable" and "good to use" is whether you counted yourself in.
You don't have to wait for something to fully break before you're allowed to be comfortable.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by writing on how chronic self-discounting erodes self-esteem; rewritten as an original scene about underpricing your own secondhand listings and your own salary

zh-tw.content:
同一款包，別人標八百，你標三百五，還加一句「可小議」。
你怕沒人要，所以先幫對方殺一次價。
談薪水也是，開口前自己先砍一刀，
免得被說獅子大開口。
你標價的方式，就是你看自己的方式。
下次先照行情寫，再讓別人來議。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又打上「便宜賣、急」之前看。下次先查一次同款的成交價，照那個數字填，不要提前幫還沒出現的人打折。
variations: 先自己降價，換不到比較快的成交，只換到比較低的自我評價。
你可以標一個你覺得合理的數字，等待本來就是價格的一部分。

en.content:
Same bag: someone else lists it at forty dollars, you list yours at eighteen and add "open to offers."
You're scared nobody will want it, so you haggle yourself down before anyone asks.
You do it with salary too — you shave a chunk off your number before you say it out loud, in case someone thinks you're asking too much.
How you price things is how you see yourself.
List it at what it's worth and let them make the offer.
en.editorNote: For right before you type "cheap, must go." Look up what the same thing actually sold for and use that number. Don't discount for buyers who haven't even shown up yet.
variations: Cutting your own price doesn't get you a faster sale. It gets you a lower opinion of yourself.
You're allowed to name a number you think is fair. Waiting is part of the price.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 psychology writing on small daily habits that build self-worth; rewritten as an original scene about deleting your own photos first when storage runs out

zh-tw.content:
容量剩下兩 GB，你開始清相簿。
風景留著、食物留著、跟別人的合照也留著，
第一個被刪掉的，是你自己那三十七張連拍——
你說「反正每張都很醜」。
清完一輪，一整年的相簿裡幾乎找不到你。
你不是不上相，你只是還沒同意自己出現。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又長按自己的照片、手指停在垃圾桶上的時候看。今天挑一張你本來要刪的，留下來就好。
variations: 拍得醜的那張，是你那天真的在場的證據。
你也可以是自己相簿裡出現最多次的那個人。

en.content:
Two gigs left, so you start clearing out your photos.
Landscapes stay. Food stays. Group shots with other people stay.
First to go are the thirty-seven burst shots of your own face — "I look bad in all of them anyway."
One cleanup later, you're barely in your own year.
You're not unphotogenic. You just haven't given yourself permission to show up yet.
en.editorNote: For when your finger is hovering over the trash icon on a photo of yourself. Keep one you were about to delete. Just the one.
variations: The unflattering one is proof you were actually there that day.
You're allowed to be the person who appears most often in your own photo library.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 self-compassion material on treating setbacks as conditions to adjust rather than evidence of personal failure; rewritten as an original scene about troubleshooting a plant versus indicting yourself

zh-tw.content:
前三盆都養死了。
你沒有下結論說自己沒天分，
你只是把第四盆搬到有光的窗邊，水少澆一點，
它就活了。
換成你自己的事，你的第一句話卻是「我就是不行」。
有時候不是你長不好，
是位置不對、光不夠、或者澆太多。
先換一個條件，再看一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又用「我就是這種人」把自己結案的時候看。今天先別檢討個性，只檢討一個條件：睡眠、光線，還是身邊那幾個人。
variations: 同一個人換個環境，常常會長成完全不同的樣子。
先調條件、再下結論——這是你對植物的耐心，也可以留一份給自己。

en.content:
The first three plants died.
You didn't decide you have no talent for this.
You moved the fourth one to a window with light, watered it less, and it lived.
But when it's your own life, the first line out of your mouth is "I'm just bad at this."
Sometimes it isn't that you can't grow.
It's the spot, the light, or too much water.
Change one condition and look again.
en.editorNote: For when you've closed the case on yourself with "that's just how I am." Before you review your character, review one condition: sleep, light, or who's been around you lately.
variations: Same person, different environment, completely different growth.
Adjust the conditions before you draw the conclusion. You already do this for plants.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 writing on postponing your own life until you feel you've earned it; rewritten as an original scene about refusing to settle into a rented apartment

zh-tw.content:
你住五年了，那幅畫還靠在鞋櫃旁邊。
不敢釘，怕押金被扣；
不敢買沙發，想說反正會搬；
連馬克杯都挑最便宜的，因為「這裡又不是家」。
可是五年不叫暫時，五年就是你的生活。
就算是租的，你也值得在牆上留一個位置。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又把一件想做的事推到「之後安定下來再說」的時候看。今天先做不用打洞的版本：用無痕掛勾把那幅畫掛上去，或至少擺到你每天看得到的地方。
variations: 暫時的地方也可以住得認真，那是你正在過的日子，不是在等的日子。
你不用先擁有一切，才准把這裡弄成自己喜歡的樣子。

en.content:
Five years in, and that print is still leaning against the shoe rack.
No nails, in case it costs you the deposit.
No real couch, because you'll be moving eventually.
You bought the cheapest mug because "this isn't home."
But five years isn't temporary. Five years is your life.
Even rented, you deserve a spot on the wall.
en.editorNote: For when you've moved something you want onto the "once I'm settled" pile again. Do the no-drilling version today: hang it with a removable strip, or at least put it where you'll see it every morning.
variations: A temporary place can still be lived in properly. It's the life you're having, not the one you're waiting for.
You don't have to own everything before you're allowed to make a place feel like yours.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 lists of small self-love practices that include scheduling time alone; rewritten as an original scene about the last Sundays of August

zh-tw.content:
八月剩下三個星期天。
這整季你都在說「下次」——那家店、那條河堤、那部沒去看的片。
可是「下次」不會自己跑進行事曆裡。
挑一個星期天，寫上時間，寫上地點，那一格只有你的名字。
不用找伴，不用拍照，不用帶回任何有用的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你發現「有空再約」講了一整季、結果一次都沒約成的那個晚上打開。今天只做一件事：打開行事曆，選一個星期天下午，把地點打進去；到時候真的不想出門也沒關係，至少那一格是你的。
variations: 行事曆上留一格給自己，不用寫理由，那格本身就是理由。
一個人的行程也是行程，不會因為沒有人一起，就自動變成可以取消的那種。

en.content:
Three Sundays left in August.
All season you've been saying "next time" — that place, that walk along the river, the film you never went to see.
Next time doesn't put itself on a calendar.
Pick a Sunday. Write the hour, write the place, and keep the guest list at one.
No company required, no photos required, nothing useful to bring home.
en.editorNote: For the night you realize "let's do it sometime" has been your whole season and sometime never showed up. Block one Sunday afternoon now — you can still bail later, but the hour is yours.
variations: An hour held on your own calendar doesn't need a reason. The block is the reason.
Plans with yourself are still plans. They don't expire just because nobody else is coming.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the feedback-file / kudos-folder habit of saving praise for low days; rewritten as an original scene about a phone photo album

zh-tw.content:
手機裡兩千張截圖：對帳明細、優惠券、別人傳的迷因。
沒有一張是那句「還好有你」。
難過的那天，腦袋只會自動播另一卷帶子——那句很久以前的評語，你到現在還背得出來。
開一個相簿，名字隨便取。
以後誰謝謝你、誰說你做得好，就順手截下來丟進去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又想起某句很多年前的難聽話、而且整晚都繞不出來的時候。現在就往上滑訊息，找到最近一句別人真心謝謝你的話，截圖，開一個新相簿。放第一張就夠了。
variations: 你記得住每一句批評，是因為它們被重播太多次；好話也需要一個地方被放著。
這不是要你變得很正面，是難過的時候，手邊至少有另一份證據。

en.content:
Two thousand screenshots on your phone: receipts, coupons, memes people sent you.
Not one of them is the message that said "honestly, thank you."
On a bad day your head only plays the other tape — that one comment from years ago you can still quote word for word.
Make an album. Call it anything.
Next time somebody thanks you or says you did well, screenshot it and drop it in.
en.editorNote: For the night an old criticism starts looping and won't quit. Scroll up your messages right now, find the last real thank-you, screenshot it, and start the album with that. One is enough.
variations: Criticism sticks because it gets replayed. Kind words need somewhere to live too.
This isn't about being positive. It's about having a second piece of evidence within reach.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 writing on quietly putting yourself last in small daily choices; rewritten as an original scene about a box of fruit

zh-tw.content:
一盒水蜜桃，你永遠先吃有壓傷的那顆。
理由很合理：壞的先吃，不然浪費。
可是吃完那顆，下一顆又變成剩下裡面最醜的——
整盒吃到見底，你一顆完整漂亮的都沒吃到。
今天先拿最漂亮的那顆，其他的等一下再說。
沒有人在後面幫你算分數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又把最後一塊完整的蛋糕留給別人、自己夾邊邊那塊的時候讀。這禮拜買水果，切之前先挑一顆你真的想吃的。
variations: 先吃壞掉的那顆聽起來像節儉，做久了會變成習慣性把好的讓出去。
輪流也可以：這次漂亮的那顆是你的，下次的下次再說。

en.content:
Peaches in a box, and you always eat the bruised one first.
The logic is airtight: eat the bad one before it goes bad.
Except once that one's gone, the next is the ugliest left —
and the box empties out without you ever eating a good peach.
Take the best one today. The rest can wait.
Nobody back there is keeping score.
en.editorNote: Peach logic shows up at the table too: the last clean slice goes to someone else and you take the crumbly edge. Next time you buy fruit, pick the one you actually want before you cut anything.
variations: Eating the damaged one first sounds thrifty. Done long enough, it's just a habit of handing over the good one.
Alternate if that's easier: the good one is yours this round, and next round is next round.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by reporting on everyday purchases people find worth paying more for; rewritten as an original scene of hesitating in a shop aisle

zh-tw.content:
你在貨架前站了快一分鐘。
手上那瓶洗髮精貴兩百塊，是你聞了會想再吸一口的味道。
最後你還是把它放回去，拿走原本那瓶——「反正洗完都一樣。」
兩百塊除以兩個月，一天三塊。
你買的其實不是洗髮精，是每天早上那三分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又把想要的東西放回架上、然後回家在購物網站上看它三個晚上的時候。下次補貨，就升級那一項，其他照舊。
variations: 升級一樣你天天都會用到的東西，比偶爾一次的大餐更容易被自己感覺到。
不是要你亂花錢，是有些東西你天天在用，值得先除以天數再決定。

en.content:
Shampoo aisle, and you've been standing there almost a minute.
The bottle in your hand costs six dollars more and smells like something you'd take a second breath of.
You put it back and grab the usual one — "it all rinses off anyway."
Six dollars across two months is a dime a day.
You're not buying shampoo. You're buying three minutes of your morning.
en.editorNote: For when you leave the thing on the shelf and then look it up online three nights running. On the next restock, upgrade exactly one item and leave everything else alone.
variations: Upgrading something your hands touch every single day registers more than one nice dinner does.
Not an argument for overspending — just for dividing the price by the number of days you'll use it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by psychology writing on why a mispronounced name affects identity and belonging; rewritten as an original office scene about never correcting it

zh-tw.content:
新同事第一天把你的名字念錯，你當下沒糾正。
第二天更難開口，第三天就算了。
兩年過去，整間辦公室都叫錯你，
你說這種事沒什麼好計較。
可是每次被叫到，你都會慢半秒才抬頭——
因為有半秒，那個名字不是你。
名字是你從第一天就擁有的東西，
值得你花三秒鐘更正一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你已經被叫錯很久、每次想開口又覺得「現在才講很奇怪」的時候。認識新的人就從第一次講清楚；舊的那些，挑一個最好講的人先講。
variations: 「不好意思，我的名字是這樣念的。」這句話不會讓任何人難堪，只會讓對方以後少錯一次。
你可以不計較很多事，但別把自己的名字也丟進「都可以」那一格。

en.content:
A new coworker got your name wrong on day one and you let it go.
Day two was harder. By day three you'd decided it wasn't worth it.
Two years later the whole office says it wrong,
and you tell people it's really not a big deal.
But you always answer half a second late —
because for half a second, that isn't you.
Your name is the one thing you've had since the very first day.
It's worth three seconds to say it the way it actually sounds.
en.editorNote: For when you've been called the wrong thing so long that correcting it feels stranger than living with it. Say it right the first time with new people, and start with the easiest person on the old list.
variations: "Small thing — it's actually pronounced like this." Nobody is embarrassed by that sentence. They just stop getting it wrong.
You can be easygoing about plenty of things. Just don't file your own name under whatever's easiest for everyone else.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by research reviews on rumination as the mechanism between self-criticism and distress; rewritten as an original scene about carrying a ten-minute mistake all day

zh-tw.content:
你多睡了十分鐘，遲到十分鐘。
主管只回了一句「早安」。
可是你自己記了一整天：
午餐在想、開會在想、晚上躺下來又想一次。
那十分鐘在早上九點就結束了，
是你一路把它從一個房間搬到下一個房間。
它不用跟你一起下班。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你為了一件早就過去的小事、整天在心裡開重播的時候。給那件事一個結束時間，時間到就讓它留在原地。
variations: 一件十分鐘的事，代價就是那十分鐘。後面那十四個小時，是你自己加上去的。
如果今天是同事遲到十分鐘，你到中午就忘了。這個標準也可以套在自己身上。

en.content:
You slept ten extra minutes and walked in ten minutes late.
Your manager said good morning and nothing else.
You were the one who kept it going all day —
through lunch, through the meeting, one more time at midnight.
That ten minutes ended at nine in the morning.
Everything after that was you carrying it from room to room.
It doesn't have to clock out with you.
en.editorNote: For a day spent replaying something small that was over hours ago. Give it a closing time, and when the time comes, let it stay where it ended.
variations: A ten-minute mistake costs ten minutes. The other fourteen hours are something you added yourself.
If a coworker had been ten minutes late, you wouldn't remember by noon. The same rule is available to you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by self-compassion literature on over-monitoring progress and premature self-evaluation; rewritten as an original kitchen scene about dough proving under a cloth

zh-tw.content:
麵團蓋上布放著的那一個小時，
看起來完全沒有事情在發生。
可是你每十分鐘掀開來看一次，
它只會愈來愈冷。
你對自己也是這樣：
才學了兩個禮拜，就在問「我到底有沒有進步」，
一天驗收三次，驗到自己不想做了。
有些東西是在沒人盯著的時候長的。
蓋回去，晚一點再看。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你剛開始一件新的事、卻已經天天替自己打分數的時候。把檢查的間隔拉長，先讓它有時間變成什麼。
variations: 不是每一段真的有在長的時期，看起來都像在長。
把驗收改成一個月一次，你才會有時間真的做點什麼，而不是一直在量。

en.content:
The hour the dough spends under a cloth looks like nothing is happening at all.
Lift the cloth every ten minutes to check and the only thing you do is let the warmth out.
You do this to yourself too —
two weeks into something new and you're already asking whether you've gotten any better,
grading yourself three times a day until you'd rather quit.
Some things only grow while nobody is standing over them.
Cover it back up. Look later.
en.editorNote: For the beginning of anything new, when you're already scoring yourself daily. Stretch the gap between check-ins and give the thing room to turn into something.
variations: Not every stretch of real growth looks like growth while you're inside it.
Move the review to once a month. Then you'll have time to actually do the thing instead of measuring it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by general writing on assertiveness and the cost of unspoken resentment; rewritten as an original scene about things lent out and never asked back

zh-tw.content:
那本書借出去一年半了。
還有那顆行動電源、上次幫他代墊的那筆錢。
你每次想開口，都會先替對方想好理由：
他大概忘了、他最近很忙、講出來多傷感情。
可是那些東西本來就是你的，
你不是在跟他要，你只是在拿回來。
開口不會毀掉這段關係，
真正在磨損它的，是你每次想起又吞回去的那一下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你心裡有一份「不好意思開口」的清單、而且愈積愈長的時候。挑最容易講的那一項，用最平常的語氣問一次。
variations: 「欸，那本書你看完了嗎？」這樣就可以了，不用鋪陳。
你替別人想的那些理由都很合理，只是你從來沒替自己想過一個。

en.content:
That book has been out on loan for a year and a half.
So has the power bank, and the money you fronted for him last time.
Every time you think about asking, you build his excuse first:
he probably forgot, he's been swamped, it would be awkward to bring up.
But those things were already yours.
You're not asking him for something. You're taking something back.
Bringing it up won't damage the friendship.
What wears on it is you remembering and swallowing it, over and over.
en.editorNote: For when your mental list of things you're too polite to mention keeps getting longer. Pick the easiest item and ask in the most ordinary voice you have.
variations: "Hey, did you ever finish that book?" That's the whole message. No wind-up required.
Every excuse you've made for him is reasonable. You've just never made one for yourself.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by general self-love writing on making room for your own needs in group settings; rewritten as an original karaoke-room scene

zh-tw.content:
包廂裡你負責點歌、切歌、幫每個人找到他要的那一首。
你自己排的那首一直被往後推，
最後燈亮了，你說「沒關係啦，下次再唱」。
整個晚上你把場子顧得很好，
只是沒有人被派來顧你。
那三分鐘不是誰施捨給你的，是你要自己留下來的。
下一次，把你的那首往前插一格。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種每次聚會你都自動變成隱形主辦人的場合——訂位、點餐、看誰還沒吃到，忙到散場才發現自己什麼都沒享受到。下次先把屬於你的那一小段排進去，再開始照顧別人。
variations: 「這首換我。」四個字而已，沒有人會覺得你在搶。
你很會把場子弄得舒服，也可以把自己算進那個場子裡。

en.content:
In the karaoke room you're the one queuing songs, skipping songs,
finding everyone the exact track they wanted.
Your own pick keeps sliding down the list,
and when the lights come up you say, "It's fine, next time."
You held the whole night together.
Nobody was assigned to hold you.
Those three minutes aren't a favor someone owes you.
They're yours to keep. Next time, move your song up one slot.
en.editorNote: For when you become the invisible host at every hangout — booking the table, ordering, checking who hasn't eaten — and only notice at the end that you never enjoyed any of it. Slot in your own small piece first, then take care of everyone else.
variations: "This next one's mine." That's the whole sentence. Nobody thinks you're cutting in.
You're good at making a room comfortable. You're allowed to count yourself as part of the room.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by general boundary writing on over-giving without noticing the cost; rewritten as an original shared-umbrella scene

zh-tw.content:
一把傘兩個人撐，你不知不覺就往他那邊偏。
回到家脫外套才發現，右邊整條袖子都是濕的。
你不是在委屈自己，
你是偏得太順手，順手到自己在淋雨都沒感覺。
傘可以往中間拉回來一點。
照顧別人跟照顧自己，本來就不是二選一。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「事後才發現自己一直在吃虧」的時刻。重點不是從此不撐傘給別人，而是撐的時候，記得看一眼自己的那半邊有沒有淋到。
variations: 回到中間不代表你變自私，只代表兩個人都不用濕。
你會在別人淋濕的時候提醒他，也提醒自己一次好嗎？

en.content:
One umbrella, two people, and you tilt it his way without even deciding to.
You only notice at home, peeling off your jacket:
the whole right sleeve is soaked.
You weren't being a martyr.
You just tilt by reflex — so automatically that you didn't feel yourself getting rained on.
You can pull the umbrella back toward the middle.
Taking care of someone and taking care of you was never an either-or.
en.editorNote: For the moment you realize, after the fact, that you've been quietly absorbing the cost. The point isn't to stop sharing the umbrella. It's to glance at your own side while you're holding it.
variations: Recentering isn't selfish. It just means neither of you has to get wet.
You'd tell a friend their shoulder is soaked. Try telling yourself once.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by general self-love writing on people-pleasing with strangers; rewritten as an original scene about leaving a shop empty-handed

zh-tw.content:
你只是進去看看。逛了十分鐘，沒有想要的。
可是店員跟了你三步、講了兩句話，
你最後拿了一雙根本不缺的襪子去結帳，才敢走出那扇門。
你不欠他一個交代，
也不欠任何人一張「我有來過」的證明。
空手走出來不是失禮，
那只是今天剛好沒有適合你的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種為了不讓別人尷尬、就先讓自己吃虧的日常小場合。下次可以練習最短的那句：「謝謝，我再看看。」然後直接走出去，不用補理由。
variations: 「謝謝，我再看看。」講完就可以走了，後面不用接。
別人的期待不是帳單，你沒有義務每次都結。

en.content:
You just went in to browse. Ten minutes, nothing you wanted.
But the clerk followed you three steps and said two friendly things,
so you bought a pair of socks you don't need
just to be allowed to walk back out the door.
You don't owe him an explanation.
You don't owe anyone proof that you were there.
Leaving empty-handed isn't rude.
It just means nothing in there was for you today.
en.editorNote: For the small everyday moments where you eat the cost so nobody else feels awkward. Practice the shortest version: "Thanks, I'm just looking." Then walk out without adding a reason.
variations: "Thanks, I'm just looking." Full sentence. Nothing has to come after it.
Other people's expectations aren't a bill. You're not required to settle every one.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by general self-love writing on letting yourself be a beginner; rewritten as an original scene about an adult beginners' swim class

zh-tw.content:
成人初級班的名單上，最年輕的是四十二歲。
第一堂課，所有人都扶著池邊，
沒有人問誰為什麼現在才來學。
你在旁邊看了兩年，怕的其實不是水，
是怕有人在心裡說「這個年紀還在學這個」。
可是真的走進去的人，都只是想學會而已。
你不是來得太晚，你只是終於來了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種心裡想做很久、卻卡在「現在才開始會不會很奇怪」的事情上。報名表填下去的那一刻，你就已經跟看了兩年的自己不一樣了。
variations: 第一堂課本來就會很笨拙，笨拙是進度，不是丟臉。
會的人也都有過扶著池邊的那一天。

en.content:
On the roster for the adult beginners' class, the youngest person is forty-two.
First session, everyone is holding onto the wall,
and nobody asks anybody why they're only learning this now.
You watched from the side for two years.
What scared you wasn't the water —
it was someone thinking, "at that age, still learning this?"
But the people who actually showed up just wanted to learn.
You're not late. You just finally came.
en.editorNote: For the thing you've wanted to try for ages but keep stalling on because starting now feels embarrassing. The moment you fill in the sign-up form, you're already different from the version of you who watched for two years.
variations: The first session is supposed to be clumsy. Clumsy is progress, not humiliation.
Everyone who can do it now had their own day of clinging to the wall.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by general self-love writing on bracing against good news; rewritten as an original scene about rehearsing bad news during a good week

zh-tw.content:
這個禮拜什麼都很順。案子過了、家裡沒事、連車位都有。
順到第三天，你晚上躺著開始想：接下來是不是要出事了。
你在腦袋裡先把壞消息演過一次，
好像先痛一次，真的來的時候就不會那麼痛。
可是那一次，你是白痛的。
今天的順利就是今天的順利，
整份收下來，不用先分一半出去給還沒發生的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種一遇到好日子就開始緊張、覺得好運遲早要還的人。下次好事來的時候，練習只做一件事：把它記下來，然後不要往下想。
variations: 壞事真的來的時候，你自然會處理；那之前不用先排練一遍。
今天很順，可以就只是很順，不用馬上找一個「但是」。

en.content:
Three good days in a row. Project approved, nothing wrong at home, even a parking space.
By the third night you're lying there thinking: so what's coming next.
You run the bad news once in your head,
as if hurting early means it will hurt less when it lands.
It doesn't. That rehearsal cost you a night for nothing.
A good week is allowed to be just a good week.
Take the whole thing. Don't hand half of it to something that hasn't happened.
en.editorNote: For people who get tense the moment life goes smoothly, convinced the good stretch has to be paid back. Next time something goes right, do one thing only: note it, then stop the thought there.
variations: You'll handle the bad thing when it's actually here. Until then, no dress rehearsal.
Today went well. That can be the whole sentence, with no "but" attached.

items.sourceNote: Background: Tainan's 做十六歲 coming-of-age custom held on Qixi (七娘媽生), historically tied to dock workers' full-wage age; written as an original piece about milestones nobody witnessed

zh-tw.content:
台南到現在還在辦做十六歲，日子就落在七夕。
以前在港邊做工，滿十六歲那年才領得到全額的工錢，
過了那天，你在帳上才算一個完整的人。
你後來也有過那種日子：
第一次把一件很難的事扛到最後、第一次有人靠著你撐過一關。
只是沒有人敲鑼，也沒有人發一張紙給你。
那就你自己記一筆。
今晚吃好一點，替那個沒被慶祝過的你補辦一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你剛獨力完成一件沒人知道的難事之後。長大的那些時刻多半沒有典禮，能到場的人只有你自己——今天就當一次那個到場的人。
variations: 沒有人敲鑼，你就自己記一筆：那天我過關了。
你等的那句「你長大了」，可以由你自己說出口。

en.content:
Sixteen. Tainan still holds its coming-of-age rite at that age, on the night of Qixi.
Dockside kids used to draw a child's wage until then. After that day, the ledger counted you as a whole person.
You've had days like that since.
The first time you carried something hard all the way to the end. The first time someone got through a bad stretch by leaning on you.
No gong. Nobody handed you a certificate.
So log it yourself.
Eat well tonight, for the version of you nobody threw a ceremony for.
en.editorNote: For right after you finish something difficult that nobody else knows about. Most growing up happens without a ceremony, so the only witness available is you. Be that witness today.
variations: No gong, no crowd. Write the line yourself: that was the day I got through.
"You've grown up" — you're allowed to be the one who says it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by general writing on accent bias in Taiwan; rewritten as an original personal scene about filing down and reclaiming a home accent, with no political framing

zh-tw.content:
到台北的第一年，你把腔調磨掉了。
沒有人要求你這樣做。你自己聽出來的——
尾音收乾淨一點，別人就不會多看你一眼。
現在你回家，阿嬤問你一句台語，
你要在腦袋裡轉兩秒才答得出來。
那個腔還在你身上，只是很久沒被拿出來用。
下次回去慢慢講，講錯字也沒關係。
它從頭到尾都是你的東西，不用重新申請。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你發現跟家人講話開始需要「翻譯」的時候。不用一次講回流利，先從一句開始；那句卡卡的，阿嬤也聽得懂。
variations: 在外面一種講法、回家一種講法，兩種都算你本人。
今天打電話回家，試著用那個腔講完一整句話。

en.content:
First year in Taipei, you filed your accent down.
Nobody asked you to. You worked it out yourself: clip the endings, and people stop looking twice.
Now you go home, your grandmother asks you something in Taiwanese,
and you need two seconds to translate before you can answer.
The accent is still in there. It just hasn't been taken out in years.
Go slow next time. Wrong word, fine.
It was yours the whole time. No reapplying required.
en.editorNote: For the moment you notice you need a translation step to talk to your own family. You don't have to get fluent again in one go. Start with one sentence, clumsy and all.
variations: One way of speaking out there, another way at home. Both of them are you.
Call home today and get one full sentence out in that accent.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by general writing on upward social comparison (measuring your average against everyone else's best); rewritten as an original piece about an assembled rival who never existed

zh-tw.content:
你在每個認識的人身上都拿走了最好的那一項：
他的自律、她講話的樣子、另一個人的收入、還有誰的體力。
你把這些組成一個人，然後跟他比了十年。
他從來沒有存在過，可是你每天都輸給他。
那七個人，各自都有自己過不去的月份，
你只是剛好都沒在現場。
今天先還一項回去。
那份標準本來就不該由七個人共同署名。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又列出一長串「我應該要」、然後覺得自己樣樣不夠的時候。把每一項標準對回它原本的主人，你會發現那張單子沒有任何一個活人做得到。
variations: 一個由七個人組成的對手，本來就沒有人贏得了。
把標準一項一項還給原本的主人，那張單子會馬上短一半。

en.content:
Seven people. You took one best trait off each of them:
his discipline, the way she talks, someone else's salary, someone else's stamina.
You assembled them into one person and spent ten years losing to him.
He has never existed. You still lose to him daily.
All seven of them have months they barely got through. You just weren't in the room for those.
Give one trait back today.
That standard was never meant to be co-signed by seven people.
en.editorNote: For when you've written another long list of everything you should be and come away feeling short on every line. Return each item to whoever you took it from, and the list turns out to be one no living person clears.
variations: Nobody beats an opponent assembled from seven different people.
Hand the traits back one at a time. The list gets half as long immediately.

items.sourceNote: Simply Psychology 的 assertive communication 說明：被動溝通（總是配合、避免衝突）會累積 resentment。取「這些不是你的義務」的核心概念，改寫成台灣聚會場合的情緒勞動清單，場景與句子全部重寫。

zh-tw.content:
以下這些，沒有人指派給你：
把每一場快冷掉的聚會救回來。
記得所有人的生日、忌口、和誰最近跟誰不講話。
在對方開口之前先猜到他在不爽什麼。
每次有摩擦，當第一個說「是我不好」的人。
你做得很好，好到大家都以為那本來就是你的工作。
可是做得好不等於欠他們。
這一輪，先讓場子自己撐一下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合聚餐、家庭場合結束後特別累的時候看。當你整晚都在找話題、記別人的細節、當那個先低頭的人，就整份念一次。
variations: 你把氣氛顧得很好，好到沒有人記得那不是你的責任。
冷場不是你造成的，也不必每次都由你來收。

en.content:
Nobody assigned you any of this:
Rescuing every conversation the second it goes flat.
Remembering everyone's birthday, everyone's allergies, who isn't speaking to whom.
Guessing what someone is annoyed about before they say it.
Being the first to say "that one's on me" whenever there's friction.
You're good at it. Good enough that everyone assumes it's your job.
Being good at something isn't the same as owing it.
This round, let the room hold itself up.
en.editorNote: For the specific tiredness you carry out of a dinner where you did all the invisible work. Read it when you've spent a whole evening sourcing topics, tracking other people's details, and apologizing first.
variations: You kept the mood afloat so well that nobody remembers it was never yours to keep.
A lull in the conversation isn't a mess you made, and it isn't yours to clean up every time.

items.sourceNote: Annual Review of Psychology 的 self-compassion 綜述：自我慈悲是可以練習的行為，而不是天生的人格特質。本則把這個概念換成「對自己做出招待的動作」的具體生活場景，內容全部重寫。

zh-tw.content:
有人要來，你會把桌子擦兩遍、拿出那組好一點的盤子，連水果都切成好拿的樣子。
自己一個人的時候，你站在流理台前，就著鍋子把它解決掉。
那不是懶，是你心裡有一套排序：
有人看的那一餐叫招待，沒人看的那一餐叫處理。
今天把喜歡的那個盤子拿出來用。
沒有人會看到，這正是重點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合一個人住、或家人不在家時三餐隨便打發的人。下次想直接站著吃完的時候看一眼——沒人看不等於可以隨便。
variations: 你請客的時候什麼都想到了，只有自己那一餐是拿來解決的。
沒有人在看的那一餐，也可以用好一點的盤子。

en.content:
When someone's coming over you wipe the table twice, bring out the better plates, even cut the fruit so it's easy to pick up.
On your own you stand at the counter and eat straight out of the pan.
That isn't laziness. It's a ranking you keep somewhere:
a meal with a witness counts as hosting, a meal without one counts as handling it.
Use the plate you actually like tonight.
Nobody will see it. That's exactly the point.
en.editorNote: For anyone who eats standing up when they live alone or the house is empty. Read it the next time you're about to eat over the sink because it's only you.
variations: You think of everything when you host. Your own meal is the one that just gets dealt with.
The meal nobody sees is still allowed a plate you like.

items.sourceNote: Breeze 談 productivity guilt：把自我價值綁在產出上，會讓不產出的時間變成罪惡感來源。改用「產品／出貨」的比喻重寫成極短句，未引用原文任何句子。

zh-tw.content:
你不是一個需要一直更新的產品。
沒有人在等你的下一版，也沒有人在算你這一季交出了什麼。
維持原樣的那些日子，一樣算你在活。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合設定新目標、或看完一整排自我提升內容後覺得自己不夠好的時候。年中檢討、生日前後也很適合拿出來看。
variations: 不是每一年都要比上一年好，才准繼續存在。
你可以停在現在這個樣子，不用急著出下一版。

en.content:
You're not a product that has to keep shipping updates.
Nobody is waiting on your next version, and nobody is counting what you delivered this quarter.
The days you stay exactly as you are still count as living.
en.editorNote: For right after a scroll through self-improvement content, or whenever you catch yourself running personal growth like a release schedule.
variations: You don't have to out-perform last year's you to be allowed to stay.
You're allowed to stay this version for a while.

items.sourceNote: Kangaroo Minds 談 rest shame：人會覺得要先累到某個程度、或先交出成果，才配得上休息。改寫成寵物與飼主的對照場景，不使用原文的比喻或句子。

zh-tw.content:
牠一天睡掉大半天，醒著的時候也沒產出任何東西。
你還是覺得牠可愛得要命，會特地把牠的墊子挪到有太陽的位置。
沒有人問過牠今天有沒有進度，牠也從來不需要證明自己該被養。
換成你自己躺一下，心裡就開始結算：今天做了什麼、夠不夠。
家裡那隻早就懂的事，你還在學——
活著這件事本身，不用附上成果。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合養寵物的人，也適合放假在家反而更焦慮的人。當「我今天什麼都沒做」這句話冒出來的時候，拿出來看。
variations: 你不會要求家裡那隻今天要有產出，那條標準對你也適用。
光是在，就已經夠了——這件事牠比你早懂很多年。

en.content:
She sleeps through most of the day and produces nothing while awake.
You still think she's the best thing in the house, and you move her cushion into the sun.
Nobody asks her what she got done. She has never had to justify being fed.
You lie down for a while and immediately start tallying: what you did today, whether it was enough.
The cat worked this out a long time ago.
Being alive doesn't come with a deliverable attached.
en.editorNote: For pet owners, and for anyone who gets more anxious on a day off than on a workday. Read it the moment 'I did nothing today' shows up.
variations: You'd never ask the cat to justify her day. The same rule covers you.
Existing is enough. The cat figured that out years ago.

items.sourceNote: Simply Psychology 的自我慈悲說明：自我慈悲是承認困難本身，而不是把痕跡抹掉。改寫成「洗過幾百次的衣服會皺」的極短生活比喻，未引用原文任何句子。

zh-tw.content:
衣服洗過幾百次會皺，那是被穿過的痕跡，不是壞掉。
你身上那幾道也一樣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在鏡子前挑自己毛病的早上。看見痕跡，不用馬上想辦法消掉。
variations: 用久的東西會有痕跡，那叫用過，不叫壞了。
不用等到看起來全新，才准穿出門。

en.content:
Clothes wrinkle after a few hundred washes. That's wear, not damage.
Same goes for the lines on you.
en.editorNote: For mornings spent picking yourself apart in the mirror. A mark can just be a mark.
variations: Things that get used show it. That's use, not damage.
You don't have to look brand new to be allowed out the door.

items.sourceNote: Annie Wright 談「沒產出就覺得自己沒價值」：休息不需要先被賺到。取這個概念改寫成賴床十分鐘的極短場景，比喻與句子全部重寫。

zh-tw.content:
你設六個鬧鐘，只為了多躺那十分鐘。
那不是懶，那是今天唯一不用交代給誰的時間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合早上按掉鬧鐘後開始罵自己的人。那十分鐘可以留著，不用先道歉。
variations: 一天裡有一小段沒有用途，不會毀掉這一天。
多躺的那十分鐘，也算你今天照顧過自己一次。

en.content:
Six alarms, just to buy ten more minutes lying there.
That's not laziness. It's the only stretch of today you don't owe anyone.
en.editorNote: For anyone who starts scolding themselves the second the alarm goes off. Keep the ten minutes. No apology needed.
variations: One small useless stretch does not ruin a day.
Those extra ten minutes count as taking care of yourself today.

items.sourceNote: 文化部文化資產局非物質文化遺產「中元普度」條目：普度桌上會多備幾份給無人祭祀者。取這個「連沒人記得的都留一份」的文化細節當背景，寫成原創的情緒勞動場景，內容全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
普渡的桌子有個規矩：要多擺幾份，
給那些沒有人記得的。
你很懂這件事。誰吃素、誰最近心情不好、誰家裡有事，
你都記在心裡，一份一份備好。
只是那張桌子從頭到尾，沒有一份是留給你的。
今天多擺一份。
被記得的那些人裡面，也應該有你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你替所有人張羅完之後，發現自己沒被算進去的時候。
variations: 你替別人備好的那份心意，自己也收得起。
多備的那一份，這次留給自己。

en.content:
There's a rule at the mid-summer offering table: set out a few extra portions
for the ones nobody remembers.
You're good at this. Who's vegetarian, who's been low lately, whose family is going through something —
you keep track and prepare a portion for each.
It's just that nothing on that table was ever set aside for you.
Put out one more today.
Someone should be remembering you too.
en.editorNote: For the moment you finish arranging everything for everyone and realize you weren't counted in.
variations: The care you prepare for everyone else — you're allowed to accept it too.
The extra portion. Keep it for yourself this round.

items.sourceNote: Psychology Today 的 perfectionism 基礎條目：完美主義者常有 all-or-nothing 思維，一有瑕疵就想全部作廢。改寫成開學新筆記本的原創場景，句子與比喻全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
開學前買的新本子，第一頁你寫得特別工整。
第三頁開始塗改，第十頁字就歪了，
於是你合起來，等下學期再買一本乾淨的重新開始。
你對自己也是：一亂就想砍掉重練，
永遠在等下一個乾淨的起點。
沒有人是從第一頁一路工整到最後的。
接著那一頁寫下去就好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你又想把一切歸零重來的時候。從中間接下去，不用回到第一頁。
variations: 不用等一個乾淨的開始，現在這一頁就可以繼續。
工整只維持三頁，那三頁也還是你寫的。

en.content:
The notebook you bought before the term started — you wrote the first page beautifully.
By page three there are crossings-out. By page ten the handwriting has gone crooked.
So you close it and wait for next term and a clean one.
You do this to yourself: one messy stretch and you want to scrap the whole thing,
always waiting for the next clean starting point.
Nobody writes neatly from the first page to the last.
Just keep going on the page you're on.
en.editorNote: For when you want to reset everything and start over. Pick up from the middle. You don't have to go back to page one.
variations: You don't need a clean start. The page you're on works.
The neat part only lasted three pages. You still wrote those three.

items.sourceNote: Psychology Today 的 assertiveness 條目：果斷表達不需要冗長的正當化說明。取「拒絕不必附帶辯解」這個概念，寫成原創的排練說詞場景，句子全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
你在心裡排練了一整套說詞。
對方只回一個「好」。
那段話不用留到下次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你為了拒絕一件小事，先在腦中演練半小時的時候。多數人根本沒打算追問。
variations: 你準備的理由比對方想聽的多太多了。
沒被問到的解釋，就讓它留在心裡。

en.content:
You rehearsed a whole speech.
They just said "okay."
You don't have to save that speech for next time.
en.editorNote: For when you spend half an hour drafting the reasons behind a small no. Most people were never going to ask.
variations: You prepared far more reasons than they wanted to hear.
An explanation nobody asked for can stay unsaid.

items.sourceNote: Verywell Mind 談設界線：過度解釋會把界線變成可協商的請求。取這個「解釋越多越像在徵求同意」的觀點，改寫成原創的送審比喻，內容全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
理由講到第三個，聽起來就像在申請許可。
你只是要拒絕，不是要送審。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你發現自己一句拒絕後面接了一長串背景說明的時候。理由多不會讓對方更好受，只會讓你看起來還在等批准。
variations: 拒絕不是提案，不需要附上佐證資料。
第一個理由講完就可以停了。

en.content:
By the third reason, it starts to sound like a permit application.
You're declining, not submitting for approval.
en.editorNote: For when you catch yourself stacking background details behind a simple no. More reasons don't soften it. They just make you look like you're still awaiting a decision.
variations: A no isn't a proposal. It doesn't need supporting documents.
You can stop after the first reason.

items.sourceNote: Psychology Today 的 boundaries 基礎條目：依賴外部藉口會讓界線變得有條件。取這個概念改寫成「最近比較忙」這句台灣常見萬用擋箭牌的原創場景，句子全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
「最近比較忙」用久了，等你真的有空，就沒有理由不去了。
不想去也算數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你每次婉拒都借用同一個藉口的時候。把忙當擋箭牌，等於承認不忙就一定得答應。
variations: 「我不想」本身就是一個完整的答案。
別把界線押在行事曆上，行事曆會空。

en.content:
"Things are hectic lately" works until they aren't.
Not wanting to go counts as a reason on its own.
en.editorNote: For when every no you give borrows the same excuse. Leaning on being busy quietly admits that a free evening obligates you.
variations: "I don't want to" is already a complete answer.
Don't stake your boundary on your calendar. Calendars empty out.

items.sourceNote: Healthline 談討好型人格：拒絕後常出現過度解讀對方沉默的焦慮。取這個心理反應改寫成原創的傳訊等待場景，比喻與句子全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
按下拒絕之後那十分鐘，你一直盯著螢幕。
空白不是生氣，只是對方在忙別的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你傳出拒絕訊息後，開始逐字回頭檢查語氣的時候。對方的沉默通常跟你無關。
variations: 沒有馬上回你，不代表你剛剛做錯了什麼。
傳出去就放下，不用守在那裡等判決。

en.content:
The ten minutes after you send the no, you stare at the screen.
Silence isn't anger. They're just busy elsewhere.
en.editorNote: For when you send a decline and immediately start re-reading it for tone. Their silence is usually not about you.
variations: A slow reply doesn't mean you did something wrong.
Send it and put the phone down. You're not awaiting a verdict.

items.sourceNote: 關鍵評論網談沉沒成本謬誤：人常因為已經投入而無法退出。取這個核心概念改寫成原創的登山折返場景，情境、比喻與句子全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
爬到第三個涼亭，你就知道自己今天上不去了。
可是你還是往上走了兩公里，
因為出發前你跟大家說過要攻頂。
那座山明天還在，你的膝蓋只有一副。
在半路轉頭不是輸，
是你終於肯把「已經走了多少」跟「還要不要繼續」分開算。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你其實已經知道該停，卻因為先前的投入或先前說過的話而硬撐的時候。已經花掉的力氣不該擁有決定權。
variations: 先前走的那幾公里不會白費，它只是不該替你決定下一步。
今天的你可以推翻早上的你，那叫更新，不叫半途而廢。

en.content:
By the third rest hut you already know you're not summiting today.
You climb another mile anyway, because you told everyone you would.
The mountain will still be there tomorrow. You get one pair of knees.
Turning back partway isn't losing.
It's finally counting "how far I've come" and "should I keep going" as two separate questions.
en.editorNote: For when you know you should stop but keep going because of what you've already invested — or what you already announced. Spent effort doesn't get a vote.
variations: The miles behind you weren't wasted. They just don't get to pick your next step.
Today you can overrule this morning's you. That's an update, not a failure.

items.sourceNote: 2026 自我關懷討論主張「停止一直修理自己」、用公平取代懲罰。取這個觀點改寫成原創的居家清單場景，用字與句子全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
水槽裡兩個碗、沙發上一籃沒摺的衣服、桌上那疊還沒拆的信。
你把這三樣讀成「我最近整個人在垮」。
它們只是三件還沒輪到的事，不是你的體檢報告。
家亂一點，你也還是好好的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你環顧家裡一圈，就順手替自己下了人格結論的時候。家事的進度不等於你這個人的狀態。
variations: 沒做完的家事只代表今天沒排到，不代表你在退步。
先把那兩個碗洗掉就好，其他的明天再輪。

en.content:
Two bowls in the sink, a basket of unfolded laundry, a stack of unopened mail.
You read those three things as "I'm falling apart lately."
They're three chores that haven't come up yet, not a diagnosis.
A messy place doesn't mean a broken person.
en.editorNote: For when one look around the apartment turns into a verdict on your character. Chore backlog is not a status report on you.
variations: Undone housework means today was full, not that you're slipping.
Just wash the two bowls. The rest can wait its turn.

items.sourceNote: Grow Therapy 2026 心理健康趨勢提到長期低強度壓力被常態化、當事人反而最難察覺。取這個觀察改寫成原創的冰箱運轉聲比喻，句子全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
冰箱的聲音停下來的那一秒，你才發現它一直在響。
有些累也是這樣：跑得很久、很低、很平均，
低到你把它當成安靜。
你不是不夠堅強才覺得撐，
是那台從來沒有關過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在你說不出哪裡累、卻已經累很久的時候。先承認它一直在運轉，才有辦法讓它停一下。
variations: 你聽習慣的那個聲音，不代表它不存在。
關掉一個小時，你會嚇一跳原來一直這麼吵。

en.content:
The second the fridge cuts out, you notice it had been humming the whole time.
Some kinds of tired run like that: long, low, perfectly even.
Low enough that you filed it under quiet.
You're not weak for finding it hard.
That motor never once switched off.
en.editorNote: For when you can't point to what's draining you but you've been drained for months. Naming the hum is what lets you shut it off.
variations: A sound you got used to is still a sound.
Turn it off for an hour and you'll be shocked how loud it was.

items.sourceNote: 2026 自我疼惜主題談接受他人照顧時的罪惡感與心理阻力。取這個角度改寫成原創的計程車對話場景，台詞與情境全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
「妳先閉眼睛休息一下，到了我叫妳。」
司機講完就把廣播轉小聲。
你「嗯」了一聲，然後整趟路都醒著，連姿勢都沒換。
不是不累，
是你不太會收下一段不用還的好。
對方已經決定要給了，你只要閉上眼睛。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在有人主動對你好、你卻忙著婉拒或盤算要怎麼回報的時候。接受，本身就是一種對自己的善待。
variations: 被照顧一下不會欠誰，你可以先收下，之後的事之後再說。
不是每一份好都要當場結帳。

en.content:
"Close your eyes for a bit. I'll wake you when we're there."
The driver turns the radio down.
You say okay, then stay awake the entire ride without even shifting position.
It isn't that you're not tired.
You just don't know how to take something you don't have to pay back.
He already decided to give it. Your only job is to close your eyes.
en.editorNote: For when someone is kind to you and you're busy deflecting it or calculating how to repay it. Letting it land is its own act of self-kindness.
variations: Being looked after doesn't put you in debt. Take it now, sort it out later.
Not every kindness needs settling at the counter.

items.sourceNote: 2026 職場心理健康專文提到「預期性自責」——在事情發生前先假設自己有錯。取這個概念改寫成原創的辦公室情境，人物與台詞全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
同事說老闆找你，你從座位走到辦公室那二十步，把上個月做過的事全部翻了一遍，還想好了要先為哪一件道歉。
結果他要問的是，你願不願意接下半年那個案子。
那二十步裡沒有人在指控你，只有你自己在開庭。
下次先走過去，聽完再決定要不要認。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在被主管、家人或朋友叫住，還沒聽到內容就先假設自己做錯的時候。等對方把話講完，是一種基本的公平。
variations: 在對方開口之前，你沒有義務先認罪。
先聽完，再決定這件事跟你有沒有關係。

en.content:
A coworker says the boss wants to see you, and in those twenty steps you review every single thing you did last month and pick which one to apologize for first.
Turns out he wants to know if you'll take the project for the second half of the year.
Nobody was accusing you in those twenty steps. You were just holding court against yourself.
Next time, walk over, hear the whole thing, and then decide whether to plead anything at all.
en.editorNote: For when someone calls you in and you've already assumed you're in trouble before hearing a word. Letting them finish is basic fairness to yourself.
variations: You are not required to confess before anyone has made a charge.
Hear it out first, then decide whether it's even about you.

items.sourceNote: 《心理界限》書評談到習慣把自己的需求排在所有人之後。取這個主題改寫成原創的訂票情境，細節與結語全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
回程的票，全家只有你的還沒買。
去程你一次劃了四張，阿嬤的敬老票挑靠走道，弟弟怕塞車你幫他改早一班，連接駁公車的時刻表都截圖丟進群組。
輪到自己你就說再看看，反正一個人比較好喬。
排在最後面的那個人也需要一個位子，現在就把它劃下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在家庭出遊、返鄉或聚會前，發現自己把所有人的事都安排好、唯獨自己那份還懸著的時候。
variations: 「一個人比較好喬」講久了，就變成一個人可以不用被安排。
把自己的那張也劃進去，這趟才算全家都有位子。

en.content:
Everyone in the family has a return ticket except you.
You booked four seats for the trip out, picked an aisle seat for Grandma, moved your brother to an earlier train because he worries about traffic, and screenshotted the shuttle timetable into the group chat.
When it's your turn you say you'll figure it out later, since one person is easy to squeeze in anywhere.
The person at the back of the line needs a seat too, so book it now.
en.editorNote: For the days before a family trip or a holiday, when you notice everyone's arrangements are settled except your own.
variations: "I'm easy to squeeze in" eventually means nobody makes room for you.
Book your own seat too. That's when the whole family is actually covered.

items.sourceNote: 身心診所談界線的入門文章提到「縮小自己以免打擾別人」的模式。取這個概念改寫成原創的租屋場景，具體細節與收尾全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
你在自己租的地方看影片會戴耳機，就算整層樓只剩你一個人。
講電話走到樓梯間，半夜煮個麵也把抽油煙機轉到最小，怕聲音穿過牆。
房租是你在付的，隔壁那戶到現在都不確定這間有沒有住人。
今天把耳機拿下來，音量開到你聽得舒服的位置。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在發現自己連在家都活得像客人的時候。基本的音量、燈光、活動範圍，本來就包含在你付出去的那筆錢裡。
variations: 把自己縮到沒有聲音，不會讓你比較好相處，只會讓你比較不在。
你住的地方，本來就可以聽得出來有人住。

en.content:
You wear headphones to watch things in your own rented place, even when the whole floor is empty.
You take calls in the stairwell, and when you cook noodles at midnight you turn the range hood to its lowest setting so the sound won't carry through the wall.
You're the one paying the rent, and the neighbors still aren't sure anyone lives in that unit.
Take the headphones off tonight and set the volume where it's actually comfortable.
en.editorNote: For when you realize you live like a guest in your own home. Basic volume, light, and elbow room are already included in what you pay.
variations: Shrinking until you make no sound doesn't make you easier to live near. It just makes you less there.
The place you live in is allowed to sound lived in.

items.sourceNote: 自我疼惜與耗竭的專文指出照顧他人時最先被略過的是自己最基本的生理需求。取這個角度改寫成原創的擬人化短篇，語氣與句子全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
如果你的水壺會講話，它今天大概會說：都下午四點了，我還是滿的。
你替三個人跑了腿，回了十幾則訊息，午餐是站著吃完的。
它一直放在你手邊，伸手就拿得到。
先喝三口，那些事跑不掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在忙到一個段落、才發現自己一整天沒喝水沒好好吃飯的時候。最低限度的照顧不用排隊等有空。
variations: 最基本的那幾件事，不用等到你把別人的事做完才輪到。
喝一口水花不到十秒，那十秒不會拖垮任何進度。

en.content:
If your water bottle could talk, today it would say: it's four in the afternoon and I'm still full.
You ran errands for three people, answered a dozen messages, and ate lunch standing up.
It's been sitting right next to you the whole time, within arm's reach.
Take three sips. The rest of it isn't going anywhere.
en.editorNote: For the moment you come up for air and realize you haven't had water or a real meal all day. Bare-minimum care doesn't need to wait in line.
variations: The most basic things shouldn't have to wait until everyone else's list is done.
A sip of water costs ten seconds. Ten seconds won't sink anything.

items.sourceNote: 2026 談「休息不需要先賺來」的文章指出許多人需要外部理由才允許自己停下。取這個核心改寫成原創的颱風假情境，台灣脈絡與句子全部自寫。

zh-tw.content:
颱風假宣布的那一分鐘，群組裡在傳貼圖，你打開筆電說先把明天的做掉。
那不是勤勞，是你需要一個夠大的理由才敢停下來——風要夠強、雨要夠久、要有人幫你決定。
外面整座城市都停了，只有你還在跑。
這一天是天氣替你請的假，收下來就好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在颱風假、連假或臨時多出來的空檔，卻忍不住想把工作往前做的時候。休息不用等到有正當理由才成立。
variations: 不必等到風夠大，你才有資格關掉電腦。
多出來的這一天沒有附帶條件，不用先做點什麼才敢用。

en.content:
The minute the typhoon day is announced, the group chat fills with stickers and you open your laptop to "get tomorrow's work out of the way."
That isn't diligence. It's that you need a big enough excuse before you'll let yourself stop: strong enough wind, long enough rain, someone else making the call.
The entire city outside has come to a halt, and you're the only thing still running.
The weather took the day off on your behalf, so just take it.
en.editorNote: For a storm day, a long weekend, or any unexpected gap you immediately want to fill with work. Rest doesn't need a justification to count.
variations: You don't have to wait for the wind to get strong enough to close the laptop.
The extra day comes with no conditions. You don't owe it any output first.
